A fourth callback, 0x72106C (copies node +0x18 dwords from the block to node +0x1C and sets node +0x19 = 1), is installed at 0x72117D. The stream fill at 0x7260A1–0x7260CB calls
    slot +0x2C with 7 parameters, the writer 0x727030 between the two calls, and
    slot +0x4C with 4 parameters, on the buffer at 0x8B4780 (the slot names are
    inferred from the COM order and parameter counts), and the call-site
    arguments agree with that order (verified): Lock (+0x2C) takes this and 7
    arguments, Play (+0x30) is called as (0, 0, 1), GetStatus (+0x24) takes one
    out pointer, Unlock (+0x4C) takes 4 arguments and Restore (+0x50) takes none.
    The EXE carries no vtable names, so the slot names stay inferred. No call
    through +0x3C (SetVolume), +0x40 (SetPan) or +0x44 (SetFrequency) has the
    stream buffer [0x8B4780] as its receiver (verified). Its 19 references are 13
    reads (Release, GetCurrentPosition, Lock, Unlock, Play, GetStatus, Restore),
    the CreateSoundBuffer out pointer at 0x725B5B, and 5 stores of null (0x725B2D,
    0x725BC4, 0x725DCE, 0x725F1C, 0x725FE3). The stream code 0x725A85..0x7263B5
    has no +0x3C, +0x40 or +0x44 call, and neither does 0x700000–0x77FFFF. The
    stream buffer has dwFlags 0x18000 (DSBCAPS_GLOBALFOCUS |
    DSBCAPS_GETCURRENTPOSITION2, stored at 0x725B63), with no CTRLVOLUME, CTRLPAN
    or CTRLFREQUENCY bit, so no hardware gain is set on it (verified). The gains
    are most likely applied in software (inferred; the mixing code is not traced
    here).
    Traced since (verified in SPEED2.EXE unless marked Open or Inferred):
    The stream buffer is created in the procedure at 0x725A85. Its DSBUFFERDESC
    has dwSize 0x24 (stored at 0x725B60), dwFlags 0x18000 (stored at 0x725B63)
    and lpwfxFormat set to the 16-bit WAVEFORMATEX built on the stack. It is
    created by CreateSoundBuffer ([0x8B4778]+0xC, call at 0x725BAE) with the
    output pointer &[0x8B4780] (pushed at 0x725B5B). Before that, the primary
    buffer ([0x8B477C]) gets SetFormat (+0x38, call at 0x725B13). Its reads are at
    0x725B07 (that SetFormat), 0x725BCB and 0x725F22 (Release). It is also the out
    pointer of CreateSoundBuffer at 0x725E76 (pushed at 0x725E64, in the procedure
    at 0x725DB5) and at 0x72605C (pushed at 0x72604A), and it is zeroed at 0x725DC8,
    0x725BDA, 0x725F31 and 0x725FDD.
    The DirectSound setup just before the pump (0x72601A..0x7260E0) is inside the
    procedure at 0x725F52, whose ret is at 0x7260F6. It calls
    SetCooperativeLevel ([0x8B4778]+0x18, call at 0x72602F), then
    CreateSoundBuffer ([0x8B4778]+0xC, call at 0x72605C) with a DSBUFFERDESC whose
    dwSize is 0x24 (0x726046) and dwFlags is 1 = DSBCAPS_PRIMARYBUFFER (0x726056).
    The output pointer is stored at 0x8B477C (pushed at 0x72604A). The stores to
    both slots at 0x725DC8 and 0x725DCE write zero (edi is zeroed at 0x725DBF), so
    the buffer the pump locks, [0x8B4780], is the stream buffer from 0x725A85,
    which the setup calls at 0x72607C. The vtable order is the DirectSound one
    (inferred from the arities).
    The stream pump is the REA procedure at 0x7260F7 (its first compare is at
    0x726100). It does nothing when [0x8B4778] is null. With the buffer-lost
    bit (2) clear and the counter DAT_008B47C0 below 0x65 it mixes when the
    playing bit (1) is set, and calls Play (+0x30, flags 1) when it is not;
    otherwise it calls Restore (+0x50). It reads GetStatus (+0x24, call at
    0x72611A) and GetCurrentPosition (+0x10, call at 0x72614E). Each wrap
    segment of nonzero length is locked (+0x2C, call at 0x726268, 7 arguments
    after this), passed to 0x725C8E(pointer, frames), and unlocked (+0x4C, call
    at 0x72629C). There are at most two segments.
    0x725C8E calls the AEMS code (0x721E13, 0x721DE6; not traced), then
    0x729574(pointer to pointer, frames), which renders blocks of up to 0x100
    frames and calls 0x7292BC(channel pointers, frames) for each block. In
    0x7292BC, in order: (1) for each aux i whose entry at 0x8B4804 + 4i is
    nonzero and whose pending float at 0x8B4924 + 4i is nonzero, 0x72886C adds
    that float into the bus [0x8B47C4 + 4i]; (2) for each channel c, 0x727030
    (memset of frames × 4 bytes; call at 0x729326) zeroes the bus whose pointer
    is at 0x8B48F0 + 4c, then if the pending float at 0x8B490C + 4c is nonzero,
    0x72886C adds it into that bus; (3) the voice loop; (4) the post hook at
    0x8B4800, when set; (5) for each channel c, vtable +0 of the object at
    [0x8B4928 + 4c] is called with (frames, bus, channel pointer, 0), after an
    optional call on the object at [0x8B4940 + 4c] (its role is not traced).
    Voice loop: voices are 0x5C bytes from 0x8B4A00 (count at 0x8B47F8), state
    byte 2 = active. For an active voice, vtable +0 of the object at +0x40 is
    called with (count, the buffer pair at 0x8B48D0 and 0x8B48D4, 0) and
    returns the frames written; voice +0x3C takes the last float of the 0x8B48D4
    buffer. For each channel c with a nonzero float at voice +0x1C + 4c, the mix
    kernel [0x8B4A04] is called with (count, gain, the 0x8B48D4 buffer, bus c +
    skip). For each active aux i whose gain (read through the pointer at voice
    +0x38, indexed by i) is nonzero, the same kernel is called into
    [0x8B47C4 + 4i]. The kernel body and the skip count (0x728B48) are not
    traced.
    0x729574 renders through the planar channel pointers (0x8B4908 + 2·frames·c)
    and calls 0x72CD6A(frames, count, map, planar base, output pointer) (call
    at 0x729638, its only direct call) only when the flag at 0x8B47FA is
    nonzero. 0x72CD6A interleaves 16-bit samples for 2, 4 or 6 channels with
    the map bytes {1,0}, {3,0,2,1} and {4,1,0,5,3,2} (read from the stores in
    0x729574); other counts write nothing. When the flag is zero, 0x729574
    copies 0x8B47F9 consecutive dwords from its argument into a local array of
    output pointers and renders into them directly.
    The flag 0x8B47FA is read at 0x728DCB, 0x729147 and 0x72957E. No
    instruction stores to it by absolute address, and 0x8B47F8 lies past the
    file data of its section (the va.py read fails), so the flag is zero at
    load (inferred from the PE layout). Which branch the game takes is Open;
    the channel count at 0x8B47F9 has no absolute-address store either, so its
    writer is Open.
    0x72886C(p, bus) adds p times w[k] into bus[k] for k = 0..15, with w[0] =
    16/17 (table entry 0x7C6A20, fmul at 0x728876) down to w[15] = 1/17 (0x7C69E4,
    fmul at 0x728946), and then sets p to 0.
    0x728957(g0, g1, in, out), with 16 floats each, adds in[k] times
    (g0 + (k+1)·(g1 - g0)/17) into out[k] for k = 0..15 (the 1/17 is the
    constant at 0x7C69E4). It is one 16-sample gain ramp, not a two-input mix.
    REA lists its calling procedures as 0x72655A and 0x728B48; the call sites
    are 0x726671, 0x726717, 0x728C11 and 0x728C9D. The gains the callers pass
    are not traced.
    The four callbacks 0x72102C, 0x72103A, 0x721046 and 0x72106C are registered
    callbacks whose caller is not traced; offsets are from the second argument
    (the dispatcher's node pointer, not re-traced). 0x72102C stores block[0] at
    +0x18, the count for 0x72106C. 0x72103A stores the constant 1 at +0x10, the
    count for 0x721046. 0x721046 copies that many block dwords to +0x14 onward,
    and 0x72106C copies the dwords counted at +0x18 to +0x1C onward.
    0x72A164 is a constructor (vtable 0x72A138 at +0; its second argument is
    stored at +0x1C). It computes no gain.
    0x5F1170 returns a float10 in st0: the minimum of the FUN_0043CE10 values
    at +0x80 and +0x90, plus, where its mode test does not return early (the
    test reads DAT_0089CF69, DAT_008669F4, DAT_00866A14 and +0x14), those at
    +0xA0 and +0xB0 (and +0xC0 and +0xD0 when +0x14 is 5 or more). FUN_0043CE10
    is not traced, so "distance" is Inferred.
    **Open**: the ramp endpoints g0 = [V+0x34][i] and g1 = [V+0x38][i] (V: the
    voice record, see Mixer channel law) are passed to 0x728957 at 0x728C11
    (also called at 0x726671, 0x726717 and 0x728C9D). 0x728957 is not traced
    (the candidates for the azimuth and pan to L/R law). The channel count
    (0x8B47F9), the flag (0x8B47FA) and the pump's buffer (0x8B4780); how the
    +0xA8 distance becomes a level (0x5F1170 returns a minimum in st0, above);
    the AEMS sound-player node and the object at 0x8B4928. The voice gains are
    traced now (writers 0x72905D and 0x729087, snapshot 0x728F75; Audio,
    "Mixer channel law"). Not ported: the law is not fully traced.
    The water drum's extra start (verified from the disassembly at
    0x46AE00, material 5; Ghidra has no procedure there): after the call
    to 0x46A540 (its role is not traced), when +0x140 is 5, the record at the
    object's +0x144 has
    byte +0x505 non-zero and +0x50C clear (the function sets +0x50C to 1;
    nothing in it clears it), up to three requests are queued by 0x7358C0 at
    0x82C6B4 (the layers use 0x82C5E0). Each is a 0x20-byte node from
    0x457E20 with kind 3, sound 0, level 0, pitch 0, azimuth 1, delay 0 and
    +0x1C 0, stored at the object's +0x14C, +0x150 and +0x154 where the slot
    is empty (a failed allocation stores 0; a refused queue calls 0x735840
    with 0x7EDD58 and retries once). +0x505 (the prop knocked loose,
    0x5ADFA0) and the requests' per-frame level (0x481FD0) are traced in
    **Sound round 12**, which ports the splash.
    The +60 condition (verified, 0x47A770, the class 0 track sample): when
    the car at object +0x118 has +0x18 with +0x58 = 6, the volume byte gets
    +60 (at most 127) before the level is read. Car +0x18 is the player
    object (only a human's car has one) and its +0x58 the camera event
    kind (see **Crash cameras and slow motion**): 6 is the crash camera
    (the jump camera, 7, gets nothing). The +60 moves only the sample
    choice (the level group of kinds 2–6); the layers' volume is the
    record's. **Ported** 2026-11-01: `CarState::crash_camera` (the
    player's `EventCameras::kind` = 6, set each race frame) →
    `collision::Impact::crash_camera` → `play`'s level.
    The 10-object cap (**open**): the count gate (`cmp [ecx+0xC], 0xA` at
    0x481D4B, `jge` at 0x481D4F) returns when `9 < [S+0xC]`, where S is M+0x3C
    and M is the pointer at 0x82B884. 0x483E20 reloads ecx from +0x3C
    (0x483E29) before its `jmp 0x481CD0` (0x483E2C), and the list walk leaves
    ecx unchanged. The zeroing at 0x458634 is in M's constructor (0x4585A0),
    not S's, and S's constructor was not traced.
    No inc, dec, or add or sub of 1 on a non-esp [reg+0xC] was found in
    0x450000–0x5BFFFF, but add and sub of registers through [ecx+0xC]
    (0x6A0346, 0x6A0367, 0x700C7B, 0x700CBD) and 274 DWORD mov writes through
    [ecx+0xC] were not traced to S, so whether S+0xC reaches 10 is open. The
    global count is 0x82B944: +1 on each insert (0x481E13–0x481E21), −1 on
    each unlink (0x481C82, 0x469D98); the gate does not read it. One object
    per record holds (0x481CD0's key test on the list at +0x24).
  * Attached models and effects (traced, **not ported**): the info's +0x84
    / +0x88 hashes are gathered at load (0x5B4230) by 0x48B8B0 from the
    emitter manager 0x8357E0's list (+8): every entry whose description
    (+0x1C) has that hash at +0x10 is copied (0x48B830: 0xD0 bytes, the
    name at +0x90 and its hash at +8, the description, the matrix at
    +0x40) into the info's lists +0xF8 / +0xF0; a prop body copies them
    again into +0x4F4 / +0x4FC (0x5B1550, each +0x10 = 1); 0x5ADB30 sets
    each one's matrix to the prop's, and on first moving (0x5ADFA0, once:
    +0x505) each +0x4FC one is started by 0x48BC50, which queues it on
    the manager's list with a start delay drawn from its description's
    +0x2C / +0x30 (type 0) or +0x24 / +0x28 (type 1; type 2 is dropped).
    L4RA: `ZCS_BarrelFireA` +0x88 0x64C2C940, `ZCS_Barrel_A` +0x88
    0x95C9F5FA, `ZCS_WaterBarrel` +0x84 0x95C9F5FA / +0x88 0x95C9F5FB,
    `ZCS_XO_GreenHDoor_00` +0x88 0xE84348EA; the rest have neither.
    (Earlier notes said the `XO_BulletSS` / `XO_TableSS` kinds have +0x88
    = 1; they have 0.)
  * The `XO_BulletSS_nn` / `XO_TableSS_00` kinds (L4RA: 12 and 1) have one
    hash at +0xA0 (0x722DB2FC, 0x5CB9A13C), resolved at load (0x5B0F21)
    to the info with that key at +0x90; no L4RA placement uses them, and
    no reader of +0x90..+0x9C was found (none of an info in the prop code
    0x5AD000..0x5B4FFF; open: what the parts do).
* **Car modes** (car +0x38): crash mode (0x5A49B0 each frame) turns off
  rest and angular damping (+0x150, +0x154), sets gravity 11 (0x7FC084),
  the aero factor (+0x30, multiplying drag and downforce in 0x59E630) to 0
  and the surface drag to 1, and holds the gas at 0.4 before the throttle
  is set (0x5A49B0 runs before 0x5ABC00). It ends in the mode update
  (0x5FC060): after 0.1 s with all four wheels down and no contact (a
  contact or lifted wheel restarts it). Mode 2 (in contact) has the
  normal physics.
* **Ground inertia** (rigid body +0x158, 0x5A49B0): the rigid body keeps
  two inverse inertias (0x59B950): +0x170 from the record's tensor and
  +0x1B0 with its yaw term × record +0x270 (2.0–2.28 for the stock cars;
  scaled by the race tunes' t4). Outside crash mode with a wheel down it
  uses +0x1B0 — in ω = I⁻¹L (0x59C600), the rolling constraint's yaw
  acceleration (0x5ABE00 at 0x5AC053) and contacts (0x593A50) — else
  +0x170; switching to +0x170 divides L.z by the factor (switching back
  does not). (Earlier notes said nothing in the physics reads +0x270.)

## Chase camera (verified except where noted)

* The camera factory 0x5F1FE0 builds type 1 for racing: constructor
  0x451660, vtable 0x787F28, update 0x453570.
* World push (**verified**, 2026-10-28; `chase::keep_out`): for kinds 0,
  1 and 5, after the shake, 0x453570 calls 0x444530: from the car body's
  centre (car +0x50 + rotated body +0x110, the box's middle; see the last
  step below) to the eye it gathers the world polygons around the
  segment (0x5E6FB0: midpoint, half-size (length + 1) / 2 + 0.5, with the
  car's barrier groups copied from car +0x8B4 / +0x8B8), then 0x444190:
  the nearest crossing of the segment with a polygon (0x5D3A00(1, 1, …,
  0.7, 1) → 0x5D3800 / 0x5D3700 / 0x5D35C0, either side) pulls the eye in
  to 0.7 m (0x7870A0) short of it; then up to three passes push the eye
  out of every polygon whose edges hold it at a distance d ∈ [0, r) on
  its normal's side by r − d, averaged (r 0.7, 0x78709C; walls the
  mover's vtable +0x30, 0x445A60: 0.7, or 3 looking back), skipping
  surfaces with the byte at 0x800EED + 0x98·s set (19, 21–28); 0x444390
  then turns the view so the car's centre keeps its screen position.
  0x444530's last step (verified, `chase::keep_out_lifted`):
  with a car, after the pushes, R = |body +0xF0 − body +0x110| + 1
  (0x5EC260 hands back the box min +0xE0 and max +0xF0, 0x5EC250 the
  box's middle +0x110, see below; 0x402CC0 reads +0xF0 − +0xE0 as the box's size,
  so +0xF0 is the maximum corner, not +0xE0 as noted before); an eye
  nearer the centre than R gets z = centre z + √(R² − its horizontal
  distance²), then 0x444390 turns the view. The box (**verified**
  2026-11-01, by 0x5AE530 and live reads of the player's 206 under
  Wine): the hull's vertices relative to the centre of mass (the shape's
  +0x40 = record +0x110, 0x5AEC30); body +0x110 is the middle of their
  bounds (0x5A1A00), **not** the centre of mass, and +0xE0 / +0xF0 their
  minimum / maximum with 0 included (the loop starts its extremes at 0).
  Live: (−2.2268, −0.8421, −0.1058) / (1.6394, 0.8440, 0.9465) / (−0.2937,
  0.0010, 0.4203), the same per car type in every car of the list. So R =
  |+0xF0 − +0x110| + 1 = 3.174 m on the 206 (the clone had |hull max −
  centre of mass| + 1 = 3.073). The sweep's centre (0x4445A5) is car +0x50
  — the car's origin, the centre of mass less the turned record offset
  (live: +0x60 − rows · (0.3, 0, 0.3)) — plus +0x110 turned by the rows
  (+0x90): 0.59 m further back and 0.12 m higher than the clone's centre
  of mass on the 206. Clone: `chase::body_box`, `Drive::push_camera`.
  Then 0x44B040(matrix, car, 1) at 0x453BDD (**verified**): not a
  push but a lift. 0x44AC10 walks the world list 0x890080 for a car (not
  the camera's own; flag 1: traffic only, owner kind [+0x14]+4 = 3; drawn
  +0x550; in the view's mask +0x5B4) whose origin +0x50 is under 12 m
  (0x7870C8) from the eye; outside flow state 6 (0x571260) a car moving
  over 15 m/s (0x7870C4) relative to the camera's car (+0x70) is passed
  over when neither the eye-to-car nor the own-to-car direction dots 0.8
  (0x7870C0) or more with that motion; the eye must be within R = |body
  +0xF0 − +0x110| + 1 of the origin and its z inside the z-range of the
  box's 8 corners (rows +0x90, origin +0x50) ± 0.5. While one is found,
  eye z = √(R² + 0.1 − dx² − dy²) + origin z; then 0x444390 re-aims at the
  camera car's +0x50 (0x7EB5C0 = the car's id, −1 without). Clone:
  `chase::lift_over_traffic`, called by `Drive::chase_view_lifted` after
  `push_camera` with the drawn traffic (free roam's, the race's unpaused;
  flow state 4 / 7 there, so the moving-car test runs) on every world
  update. The eye heights near walls were not re-measured against
  the original after the fix. The shake's noise clock is the world
  clock's tick (0x865188 × 0.00025, `ChaseCamera::set_clock`) and the
  nitrous flame (stage set, `carfx::purging` false) feeds
  `ChaseCamera::set_nitrous_flame`, both per world update.
* Each car type has its own camera table at record +0x720: two counts,
  then six 16-byte entries {i16 kind, u16 tilt (binary angle), f32 x,
  f32 z, f32 y} in car space, looked up by 0x5ECCB0 → 0x441140.
  * A second set at +0x790 is for split screen.
  * Kinds: 0 far, 1 near, 2 bumper, 3 driver, 4 hood, 5 high.
  * The 240SX's near chase is 4.7 m behind and 1.7 m up.
* Player camera setting → kind (0x502500): 0 → 2, 1 → 4, 2 → 1, 4 → 5,
  else 0. Setting 4 (Super Far) is the drift races' (verified): the
  drift set-ups (0x4FF0CC; career 0x532569 for event +0x0F = 5) set
  0x83AA74 = 4, every other set-up (0x4FEFE0, 0x4FF05F, 0x4FF146,
  0x4FF1BF, 0x53257E) turns a 4 into 3 (`Settings::race_camera`).
* Field of view per kind (0x7EB5B4): 13020 (71.5°) for the chase views and
  16384 (90°) for bumper, driver and hood. The eased angle goes to camera
  +0xC4.
* Projection (0x5C7ED0, **verified**): the camera's angle is scaled before
  its tangent is taken. For views 1, 2, 4 and 5:
  * `m00 = 1/tan(fov·1.1/2)` (0x7A27E4);
  * `m11 = −1/tan(fov·(1.1/0.8696)·(h/w)/2)` (0x7A27E8 / 0x7A27E0), where h
    and w are the target record's +0x18 / +0x14.

  Other views use factor 1 and h/w; views 9 and 10 use a fixed 0.6. On a 4:3
  screen the chase view is therefore 78.7° wide and 67.9° tall.
  **Modded captures** (2026-10-31): the Wine copies ran the
  widescreen fix with FixFOV = 1 (all but look112), which patches this
  function (0x5C7F60 / 0x5C7F71: views 1 and 4 take 1.0 for h/w, the
  mirror view 3 0.45, other views ≤ 10 1.0; 0x5C7FFA / 0x5C800C /
  0x5C8031: the y half-angle factor 0.5 → 0.43511 and the m00 / m11
  numerators 1.0 → hor3DScale (1 at 4:3) / 1.22). At 4:3 that equals the
  native m11 at the chase views' 13020 (71.5°) — free-roam edges match
  the vanilla original to the pixel — but not at other angles: the front
  end's turntable car was about 4 % taller in the modded captures (the
  turntable's front rim at y 726 / 765 against the vanilla original's
  716 / 753); hood / bumper (90°) were about 4 % flatter and the narrow
  scene lenses about 4 % taller. The clone matches the vanilla original
  (main menu rim 753 / 753). Near and
  far come from camera +0xBC / +0xC0, with far fixed at 15000 for view 1.
  `Camera::game_fov`.
* Tuning per kind is at 0x7EC610. It points to two 0xB0-byte records,
  which 0x446DC0 blends at the global 0x787154 = 0.5, so their average is
  used. Each record has:
  * ease times for the eye, look-at point, field of view and lean (+0x00);
  * lean, eye and look-at lag, each as scale / min / max vectors (+0x10,
    +0x40, +0x70);
  * ease times for the chase direction (+0xA0).
* Easing (0x5749F0): every frame, each coordinate refits a cubic from its
  value and slope to the target with zero slope, and moves dt/duration
  along it.
* The frame (0x445E00): for the chase kinds (vtable slot 9, 0x445A90) it
  faces the eased chase direction with z up. For the others it is the
  car's orientation. Its origin is the car's position.
* The chase direction (0x445C20): the velocity (mirrored when reversing)
  blended with the car's forward, from 0 at 8 m/s to 1 at 13 m/s (graph
  0x7EC420). Its vertical part fades out over 2 s. Of the mover's stamp +0x58, which 0x44DE90
  renews each update with car +0x5CC set and car +0x424 > 1 (verified, world-systems parity;
  docs/world-systems-parity.md, Cameras), not of the camera's life.
* Lag (0x44DE90): the car-space acceleration, averaged over 4 frames, ×
  scale and clamped. It is added to:
  * the eye;
  * the look-at point, which is (0, 0, x·tan(tilt) + z) for chase views
    and (x + 1, 0, z − tan(tilt)) for the others;
  * the lean, whose z is fixed at 1.

  The 4-frame average (0x446F10, called at 0x453767) reads car +0x80
  (camera +0x2C is the car, 0x5EAC80). The car's state block is car +0x40
  (0x56D393): its +0x20 position, +0x30 velocity and +0x3F0 speed
  (0x5A5550, 0x592170), +0x50 the 4×4 orientation (from the rigid body's
  +0x30), so +0x80 is state +0x40, between the velocity and the matrix.
  Its writer is 0x59B9C0, which the +0x40 scans did not cover: a vector
  helper writes the destination this +0x80 (`thunk_FUN_00441000(this +0x80,
  M, input)`, an affine transform of the 4th argument by M, where M is the
  matrix copied into this +0x30 (2nd argument) with the reciprocals of this
  +0x170 / +0x184 / +0x198 folded in; the stack layout of the diagonal is not
  fully resolved). Callers 0x5A2AD7 and 0x5A48D0 pass input = [X +0xD0] (X =
  [esi +0x30] or [esi +0x58]); 0x5A469D and 0x5ADC63 pass locals. At 0x5A2AD7
  `this` is ECX = [esi +0x20], and the input is the address X +0xD0 (a `lea`,
  the 4th argument; verified from the pushes). The callee's `this` is the car
  body B = [V +0x20] (verified: 0x5A2A70 is entered with ECX = V, and 0x5EBC10
  tail-jumps to it when [Q +0x28] == 3). 0x59B9C0 (verified) stores arg1 to
  B +0x20..0x28, arg3 (X +0x30) to B +0xA0..0xA8 and the input to B +0xC0..0xC8,
  passes arg2 (X +0x50) to a call to 0x4012B0 with B +0x30, and calls 0x43C9C0
  with destination B +0x80, a local at esp +0x80 and the input; the transform
  semantics of 0x43C9C0 and the helpers are not traced. 0x453767 (verified) calls
  0x446F10 with ECX = [camera +0x5C] and pushes [camera +0x2C] +0x80. 0x446F10
  (verified) is a ring filter: 16-byte entries at [ring +8], an index [ring +7]
  that wraps at the cap [ring +5], a fill count [ring +6] capped at that cap,
  running sums at ring +0x10..0x18, and a mean (sum times 1.0 / count, with 1.0
  at 0x784250) at ring +0x20..0x28. The cap is not traced, so "4-frame" is
  inferred. 0x453570 sets [camera +0x2C] = 0x5EAC80(camera +0x20) when camera
  +0x20 is non-null (verified). 0x5EAC80 (verified) returns [P +4] when byte
  P +0x24A is zero; otherwise, if [[0x890118] +0xBD0] is non-null, it returns the
  first dword of the object that pointer names. 0x5F1680 stores zero to [this +4]
  at 0x5F1A3E (verified on the path shown). So [camera +0x2C] is B only if P +4 is
  B for the player camera: **open**. That the input is the acceleration is
  **inferred**; the producer of X +0xD0 is not found. The
  state class does treat it as a vector of its own: the reset 0x59F890
  zeroes +0x30 (velocity) and +0x40 together before setting the matrix,
  and the serializer 0x59F530 writes +0x10, +0x20, +0x30, +0x40 (three
  floats each) and then the matrix +0x50. The vector stores at +0x40 in
  the physics range (0x5958CE, 0x596F38, 0x5980AA, 0x5B35E1, 0x5B513F)
  belong to other objects (0x5B35E1's has sub-objects at +0x224 / +0x228
  with a kind at +0x10, 0x5958CE's a table at +0xC4), not the state.
  Camera +0x2C comes from 0x5EAC80 on camera +0x20, the player object
  (constructor 0x5F1680, listed at 0x8900B4; not re-verified here): its +4, or the car at
  [[0x890118] +0xBD0] while its byte +0x24A is set. A scan of the
  whole executable for three-float stores at +0x40/+0x44/+0x48 of one
  base (any order, within 20 instructions) finds only zeroing
  constructors and resets in 0x580000–0x5C0000 (0x583258, 0x59F8A4,
  0x5A1832, 0x5B35E1, 0x5B7631, 0x5BB212, 0x5BB3ED); 0x59B9C0 is not among
  them. X's +0xD0 and +0xE0 are serialised as vectors by the CarState
  serializer 0x59F530, so X is likely the CarState.
* The chase kinds use the eased lean (x, y, 1) as up; the others use the
  car's up. Bumper and driver snap every frame.
* Shake (0x452ED0 → 0x441340, **verified** except S):
  * A row from the graph at 0x7EC430 is picked by |v| (+0x430) × 4 / S,
    S = [car +0x10] +0x20 (100 when car +0x10 is null). Car +0x10 is not
    0x5B06B0's set-up object: under Wine (circuit_s1_pinned, fields
    `setup_*`, `trap*`, docs/evidence/n-ai/) it points into a static array,
    0x890170 + 0x940 · slot (the racers' records; +0x00 the car type index,
    +0x18 the performance rating 196.70 / 195.92 / 179.79 = 0x5B4DD0's area),
    and its +0x20 read 73.7595 (206, player and rival), 67.0541 (240SX),
    75.1006 (MIATA) = exactly 55, 50 and 56 steps of 1.3410819 m/s (3 mph).
    That is **not** `handling::launch_times`' quarter-mile speed (41.5 / 41.4 /
    40.5), nor the clone's top-speed loop (0x5B5940 as `Handling::
    computed_top_speed`: 55.9 m/s for the 206, capped at the record's
    125 mph; 65.7 m/s uncapped). +0x1C (183.04 / 181.65 / 168.40) and the
    writer of +0x20 were open. **Settled** (**measured** write
    watch + **verified** formula): +0x20 is the info's performance object
    +0x10, written at 0x5B5CB5 in 0x5B5AC0 (the acceleration table's loop:
    v in 3 mph steps from 0 until the top gear passes its shift rpm, at
    most 92 steps), i.e. the gearing-limited top speed; the info is a copy
    (0x413440) of a stack-built one. The clone: `Handling::
    gearing_top_speed` (= `acceleration_curve`'s span after the race's tune,
    `handling::gearing_top_speed`) for S here, the typed replay camera's
    Speed weight and the belt's cap; the data test matches 11 stock cars
    bit for bit (`gearing_top_speed_matches_the_original`).
  * Four noise channels: sideways, up, pitch and yaw. Rates are 0x7EC480 ×
    the row's rate, and amplitudes are 0x7EC490 × the row's amplitude ×
    0x7EBE90[kind] (1.0) × 0.2 outside a drag race (0x89E7D8 / 0x890108).
    A burning nitrous shot (0x59FA40 ≠ 0 and 0x5ECDC0 = 0) adds 0.2 to
    the amplitude and takes the rate × 1.4.
  * The noise clock is the sim clock, (float)[0x865188] × 0.00025
    (`ChaseCamera::set_clock`; the clone's camera age until the game hands
    it).
  * The noise is six octaves of hashed value noise (0x441270, 0x4411B0).
  * The angles are in degrees, scaled to the field of view against 60°
    (0x4412E0).
  * The rough-surface set (0x7EC4A0 rates 3, 5, 7, 5.5; 0x7EC4B0
    amplitudes 0.007, 0.01, 0.6, 0.8): amplitude row[1] × Σ surface row
    +0x3C of the four wheels (car +0x394..+0x3A0; rows 0x800EC0 + 0x98·s)
    × 10 × 0.25 × 0x7EBEA8[kind] (1.0, no drag factor), rate row[3] × Σ
    row +0x38 × 0.25; added to the sway per channel (0x4414BD..0x4414F2).
    Asphalt's +0x3C is 0; dirt and grass 0.05, cobblestone 0.03 at rate 3.
* **Impact shake** (`chase::impact`, `Drive::impact_trigger`; **verified**
  in the disassembly, **observed** under Wine where marked). A hard change
  of the car's velocity jolts the player's view for 0.3–0.7 s.
  * Input: car +0x80 = (+0x70 − last frame's +0x520) / the world step,
    written for every car by Car_UpdateRaceEvents 0x604750 (m/s², world
    axes, once a world frame). World_UpdateControllers (0x609CF0) then
    loops over the human racers (0x60A12B, skipped in game flow state 5)
    and, for a car with a player (car +0x18), calls 0x572E60(player
    +0x10, car +0x80) at 0x60A154. The clone: `CarState::
    world_acceleration` after the player's world update (free roam, the
    race, the countdown's held step and the start scene's), not in the
    scene-driven paths (a new chase mover clears the slot after them).
  * Trigger 0x572E60: skipped when 0x5EA7D0 is true (player mover type 1
    with +0x14 set and the camera setting mapping to view kind 3 through
    0x502500 — no setting does, so never). w = car +0x80 × (0.7, 0.5,
    2.0) (0x7FB750), m = |w|; nothing below 250 (0x79DCDC); f =
    (min(m, 600) − 250) / 350; amplitude 0.08 + 0.08 f m, duration
    0.3 + 0.4 f s (0x79DCE4..0x79DCF0). It starts only when the amplitude
    is above the running shake's present curve value (0 when none runs):
    a bigger hit replaces a running shake, a smaller one only once it has
    decayed. With the player's event kind (+0x58, 0x8900AC[i]) 7 the
    amplitude is × 0.8 and the duration × 1.2. 0x572820 fills the slot
    0x865360 + i × 0x20: −amplitude · unit(w) (0x43CF90), the curve
    0x7FB7A0 (keys at 0x7FB36C: (0, 1), (0.1, 0.7), (0.3, 0.5), (0.5,
    0.4), (1, 0)), time 0, the duration, rate 17 (0x79DC70).
  * Step 0x5728D0, once a main-loop frame (0x5814C2, after the world
    update 0x581417 and the cameras 0x5814A3): time += g_FrameTime
    (0x865150, the world's step, slow motion included) / duration; at or
    past the last key (1.0) the slot's curve is cleared. A test flag
    0x8650C0 (no writer in the code) would start slot 0 with (0, 0, 0.3)
    for 0.6 s. Reset 0x5729F0: the world object's constructor 0x5FF4A0,
    0x5FF8A0 and Player_ChaseCamera 0x5FA830 with its reset flag (or no
    mover before). The clone resets on a placement (`Drive::place`) and
    the start scene's end (0x439070 → 0x5FA830(1)); the other callers of
    0x5FA830 are **not mapped** one by one (a shake lasts ≤ 0.84 s).
  * Offset 0x572870: the slot's vector × curve(time) while trunc(17 ·
    time) (0x75BED4) is even, else 0 — a strobe: at 60 fps a 0.56 s shake
    is on for 2 frames, off for 1–2.
  * Apply 0x572A60(view, matrix): only while the world's time scale
    (0x890080 +0x108, the slow motion's rate) ≥ 1 and for views 1, 2, 3
    (views 1 and 3 read slot 0, view 2 slot 1). Callers: the chase mover
    0x453570 at 0x453B55, right after its look-at (0x5BA9B0: view x =
    unit(forward × up), y = unit(forward × x) — down —, z = forward) and
    before the speed shake 0x452ED0 and the world push 0x444530, for all
    six kinds (chase, bumper, driver, hood; look-back too); the rear-view
    mirror 0x44BA80 at 0x44BE7B (view 3). Not the crash / jump camera,
    the NIS or the replay track cameras. With T = offset · V's rotation
    (the offset in the view's axes): V' = V · translate(T) · RotateX(a) ·
    RotateY(b) (D3DX row vectors, 0x63CED8), a = trunc(−1200 (T.y +
    T.z)), b = trunc(2000 T.x) binary angles (0x7FB740 / 0x7FB744; the z
    turn's factor 0x7FB748 is 0). So the eye moves by −offset (along the
    weighted acceleration) and the view pitches / turns by up to ~1°.
  * **Observed** (Wine, the parity cave at 60 fps; tools/parity
    scenarios crash_wall, impact_wall_bumper, impact_wall_150,
    prop_barrels_120; docs/evidence/impact-shake/): the slot starts on
    the frame of the contact (weighted 481, 456, 1317 and 386 m/s²), the
    view of that frame takes the full vector, the slot's time steps by
    the frame's ticks / duration and ends after 33 / 32 / 41 / 27 frames;
    view 1's eye and forward axis move as the rule gives (eye within
    7 mm of eye − offset, the turn within 0.09° of the rule's) in the near
    chase and the bumper view. A 4 m drop onto the highway at 60 km/h
    (impact_drop) stays below 250 (166 m/s² weighted): a landing shake was
    not observed.
  * The clone (`chase::impact::ImpactShake`, `Drive::impact`): the slot
    on the drive, triggered after the player's world update, the chase
    view applying it on the tick before the speed shake
    (`ChaseCamera::set_impact`), the world frame's end stepping it
    (`Drive::tick_clock`), the mirror's camera shaken by the tick's
    offset; the drawn camera blends the tick's shaken cameras between
    ticks (docs/uncapped-fps.md). The time scale and kind 7 are the
    event cameras' (`Impact::follow`): read after the slow motion's
    advance and again after the event rules, so the trigger sees the
    kind as of the frame before on the frame kind 7 starts (the clone
    runs the event rules after the cars' update; **inferred** harmless:
    kind 7 runs at time scale 0.4 for 8 s, longer than any shake).
* Not modelled: the look-back flip, and the 1.3× pull-out in special states (0x445AC0).

## Player camera movers (2026-10-29; verified unless marked)

* Camera_Factory (0x5F1FE0, player in ECX, args type and "keep the old
  mover" flag) frees or parks (+0x23C, +0x240) the player's mover +0x238
  and builds by type: 0 none; 1 the chase camera (0x451660, kind from the
  camera setting through 0x5EB410); 2 a fixed look-at (0x455B10: eye at
  the car + 4 m up); 3 0x44DBF0; 4..0x0E the event camera 0x4531A0
  (vtable 0x787D40); 0x0F / 0x10 the crash camera 0x44BEA0 (0x470 bytes,
  placed beside the road ahead from the racer's route, 0x41CE90; when
  the road sight test 0x5E7EE0 fails it builds a chase camera instead);
  0x11 0x44ED50 (vtable 0x787FC8); 0x12 the track camera 0x453C00; 0x13
  the target camera 0x4519E0 (vtable 0x787F78); 0x14 the showcase; 0x15
  the dyno camera 0x452600 (vtable 0x788070, field of view 0x32DC). It
  refuses a type equal to the current one (but 0x12), 0x11 in game flow
  state 5, and anything but 0x14 while the showcase is up (0x5012C0).
  Every mover's +0x20 is the player.
* **Look back** (`ChaseCamera::set_look_back`): the Look Back control
  (DIACTION 9, B / K) sends event 0x7E to the player (0x602BE0), held:
  player +0x249 = pressed, then the chase mover's vtable +0x14 (0x445A30)
  stores mover +0x51 (on a change it also sets 0x883E34 = 1 through
  0x5D7AF0, reader **open**). With +0x51 set, the player's +0x2B
  (0x5EB530 returns 1 when it is clear) picks one of two exclusive
  modes (the audio and camera parity 2026-11-05, re-read; the earlier note had both at once):
  * +0x2B set: the view keeps its own entry; 0x453570 multiplies the
    eased eye and look-at point by −1 in x and y (0x4539A5..0x4539BD:
    0x7842A0 = −1, else 0x784250 = 1) before the frame transform, so the
    eye is at once on the mirrored side of the car's origin; walls at
    0.7 m (0x787090);
  * +0x2B clear: the eye entry (0x445EB0) is 0x7EC400's row (−17.2, 0, 6)
    with tilt 0x787080 = 0x1450 (split screen 0x8707DC = 3: (−15.8, 0,
    4.4), 0x0DD4), not mirrored, eased; walls at 3 m (0x787094, 0x445A60).
  The player's +0x2B read 1 under Wine in free roam and a race, and every
  view looked back mirrored in the first frame (docs/world-systems-parity.md,
  Cameras); its writer (**verified**, gap sweep 2026-11-05) is the player's
  constructor 0x5F1680: it zeroes +0x20..+0x4F and sets +0x2B = 1 through
  the block's base (0x5F17A5, `mov byte [edx+0xb], 1`, edx = player +
  0x20; +0x2C = 0x755), and no other store to it was found, so the
  mirrored look-back is the only one the game uses and the 0x7EC400 row is
  dead in practice. `chase::LOOK_BACK_TABLE` = false (no behaviour change).
  Constants checked live in the running original (peek, 2026-10-29).
* **Own car hidden** (`ChaseCamera::hides_car`): 0x453570 sets view
  +0x280 to the car for the non-chase kinds unless the kind is 4 (hood)
  and not looking back; the car list's draw skips that car (0x60D584).
  So bumper and driver never draw the player's car, the hood only while
  looking back. **Inferred**: the car's shadow (queued apart, 0x6162F0)
  still draws.
* Race modes in 0x453570: in drift (0x89E7D9) and URL (0x89E7E2)
  races (or their online twins) the blended tuning's eye lag scale
  (+0x40) is zeroed; the shake's amplitude (0x7EBE90[kind], 1.0 for all)
  is ×0.2 except in a drag race (0x89E7D8). In URL races the
  eye entry is (−10, 0, 5) with tilt 0x82A4D0 (3003 live; the file holds
  1, a static initialiser sets it); a car whose +0x30 object answers its
  vtable +0x54 gets (−5, 0, 1.5) with tilt 0x82A4DC (910 live). The clone
  has no URL race (its flag is only Quick Race type 11), so that override
  is not ported.
* Event cameras (Player_StartEventCamera 0x6022F0(kind, …)): only while
  racing (race status 4), one player, not in a drift race, 5 s since the
  same kind (0.1 s for the keys): 1 → type 0x0D (key event 0x7F), 2 → 0x0E
  on a nearby object (0x455BD0; key 0x80), 3–5 slow motion only
  (0x5EA290(rate, seconds): 1/3 for 8 s, 1/3 for 2 s, 2 for 4 s; key 0x81
  is kind 3), 6 → the slow-motion camera 0x0F (0.4 for 8 s), 7 → 0x10
  (the same mover re-aimed; 0x5F1FE0 case 0x10). Kind 6 comes from
  Car_Crash (at 0x5A0105): an impact of 30 m/s or more (not in a drift
  race, the racer's +0x58 not already 6 / 7); Car_UpdateRaceEvents
  (0x604750) starts 0x0F / 0x10 itself too (0x604CD3 / 0x604FD3, with
  0x5EA290 from 0x7A5500 / 0x7A552C; its trigger is the in-air test of
  the earlier notes, not re-traced here). Both need player +0x24 ≠ 0. The events 0x7F–0x81
  have no row in the Controls menu (no default key, **inferred** from the
  DIACTION table's 18 actions).
* **Crash cameras and slow motion** (`src/event_camera.rs`,
  verified unless marked). Player +0x24 is the Jump Camera option
  (0x83AA20 = settings +0x1C, copied by the director's constructor at
  0x5F180B); kinds 1..5 need 0x83AA24 (settings +0x20, 127.5) instead. Each kind
  also needs 0x8020E8[any player's +0x58] clear (kinds 3..7 block) and
  ends a running kind 1 / 2 first (0x8020E0). Slow motion: 0x5EA290 sets
  the world's +0x108 rate, +0x10C seconds, +0x110 callback (0x6022E0 →
  0x5FFE80(1)); 0x5EA370 counts +0x10C down by the real frame time,
  then resets the rate to 1 and runs the callback, and returns frame
  time × rate — the world's step. 0x5FFE80 (end): kinds 1, 2, 6, 7
  restore the saved mover, every kind resets the slow motion, +0x5C =
  kind, +0x58 = 0. Triggers: Car_Crash (0x5A0095..0x5A0105) for a car it
  just put in crash mode — no drift race, car against car (0x592C70), the
  push ≥ 30 (0x7A186C), a human racer (0x431DD0), its director's kind
  not 6 / 7, and 0x5F1EF0: from the route node nearest the car
  (AIRoute_NearestNode on the car's route: car +0x2C's vt+0x24 = 0x418560,
  `lea eax,[ecx+0x68]` — the controller's own maintained node list, count

## Front end (verified except where noted)

The menus are FEng packages: FRONTEND/FrontB.lzc (137), GLOBAL/GlobalB.lzc
(19) and GLOBAL/GLOBALA.BUN (2). A package chunk is 0x30203 (plain) or
0x30210 (a u32 name hash, then a JDLZ or HUFF block).

* **Package** — four-character tags `tag u32, size u32`: `FEn\xE7`
  { `PkHd` (name at +0x18, then the file path), `TypS`, `Res\xCC` {
  `RsNm` NUL-separated names, `RsRq` u32 count + 24-byte requests {u32 hash,
  u32 name offset, u32 kind (0 untextured, 1 texture, 2 font), 3 × u32} },
  `Obj\xCC` { `Butn`, `FOb\xEA`* } }.
* **Object** (`FOb`) — `ObjD`, then `Scrp`* and `MsgR`*. `ObjD` and
  `Scrp` use two-character tags with a u16 size:
  * `Ot` kind (1 image, 2 string, 4 list, 5 group, 7 movie, 9 coloured
    image, 11 simple image, 12 multi image), `Oh` name hash, `OP` {id,
    name hash, flags, resource index}, `PA` parent id, `If` image flags.
  * `SA` the animatable state, 17 dwords: colour as integers B, G, R, A;
    pivot; position; rotation (quaternion); size — plus the texture
    rectangle for images (21 dwords) and corner colours for coloured images.
    The canvas's y points down and an angle turns **clockwise** on screen:
    0x51CEE0 builds the row-vector matrix [[cos, sin], [−sin, cos]], and
    UI_Sponsorship_new's SideScroll_Arrow_1 (top, −90°) must point up.
    Verified: with this sign the minimap frame's rotated arcs close into a
    ring and the turbo needle rests near 0.
  * Strings: `St` UTF-16 text as authored, `SH` label hash (`bin_hash` of
    the label, looked up in the language table), `Sj` justification, `Sl`
    leading, `Sw` wrap width, `Sb` (**verified**, 0x51C110: 1 centres each
    line on the origin and 2 ends it there; 4 centres the block
    vertically, else 8 ends it there — see Layout).
  * Flags: bit 0 is the runtime hidden bit (0x50CA00 sets it, with
    0x400000 "changed", down a group; 0x50CA50 clears it; the renderer
    skips such objects, 0x51C670; 6 shipped objects, all in HUD_Drag, have
    it set). 0x10000000 (**verified**) is not a hide bit: the `ObjD`
    reader (0x555150, test at 0x5552EC) puts every object with it in the
    package's button list (+0x90), the objects the pad moves between; the
    screens hide the buttons they do not use themselves (e.g. MC_Main's
    0x4A3460: 0x50CA00 and +0x1C |= 0x4000000, the bit that takes a button
    out of the focus order). **Verified**: nothing in the draw path tests
    0x10000000. The renderer's skip (0x51C670) reads only +0x1C bit 0, and
    the queue and renderer code in 0x51A000–0x51C8FF tests no other bit of
    +0x1C but 0x40 (0x51C870, which runs 0x50CA00 on the object and sets
    0x400000). So the game draws such a button unless the screen's code
    hid it. The clone's `hidden()` matches: only bit 0 or the screen's
    own hidden list hides, and `ScreenState::shown` keeps a bit-0 object
    on, standing in for 0x50CA50. 0x100000 marks an
    instance of a library object (0x5186C0 copies it in). A group with bit
    31 is skipped by the traversal (0x52C5E0) unless the renderer's first
    byte is set (**verified**): the renderer's constructor (0x536180, at
    0x536262) and the FEng manager's (0x5372F0, at 0x53738D, copying it to
    every package's +0x14) set it to 1, and no other write was found, so
    such groups draw — the clone ignores the bit.
* **Scripts** — `Sh` {name hash, length ms, flags, track count}; then per
  track `FI` {param type (4 vector, 6 colour), size, interpolation, —,
  length}, `To` (first `SA` dword it drives), `Kd` (the base value at time
  −1, then {time ms, delta} keys, linear); `Sc` the script chained after;
  `EV` timed messages. Names are `bin_hash`: INIT runs when a package
  opens.
  * Runtime (**verified**; `frontend::animate`, `feng::sample`). The
    reader (0x5515F0) keeps a script as +0xC length, +0x10 time (ms),
    +0x14 flags, +0x18 chain, +0x1C track count, +0x20 tracks (0x38 bytes:
    +0 param, +1 size, +2 interpolation, +3 loop mode / bit 7 "done", +4
    24-bit length, +7 first `SA` dword, +8 the base key, +0x30 the key
    list), +0x28 events, +0x30 name; an object's current script is +0x54,
    and the reader sets it to INIT (0x1744B3) directly.
  * Clock: the manager's update (0x558D89) ticks every package's objects
    (0x54CE70) in steps of at most 20 ms, then pumps the queues (0x541FD0,
    0x5559D0). 0x54CE70 adds the step to the time; at or past the length
    a chained script evaluates its end (0x541DC0), moves to the chain
    (+0x54) with the time carried over (t − length) and re-bases its
    tracks (0x517720); without a chain the flags & 3 pick: 0 hold (time =
    length + 1, then no more evaluation, so values the screen's code set
    stay), 1 loop (t mod length, re-based), 2 t mod twice the length; a
    zero-length script ends on its first step. A finished held script is
    not evaluated again (0x54D09F).
  * Tracks (0x541DC0 → 0x535500): interpolation 0 holds the key at or
    before t (0x519D40), 1 and 3 interpolate (0x52BDD0), others are not
    evaluated; the shipped packages use 1 everywhere but one track (3).
    A track with bit 7 of +3 is skipped; 0x517720 clears it when a script
    starts and 0x535500 sets it after evaluating a keyless track, so a
    keyless track writes its base once (the packages mark keyless tracks
    with it; none with keys). 0x52BDD0: 0x5052B0 finds the first key at
    or after t (else the last); f is (t − previous) / (key − previous) as
    a float (1 with no previous key or t at or past the key); the loop
    mode (+3 & 0x7F) 1 runs past the last key towards the first, reached
    at length + the first key's time (and before the first key from the
    last), 2 reflects t past the length. Values are the base plus the
    delta: floats a + (b − a)·f (0x505150); colours (and ints) a +
    ftol((b − a)·f + 0.5) (0x5051A0; ftol truncates); rotations slerp
    (0x519B00: −b for a negative dot, nlerp above 0.999, a 16-bit angle
    — a float here) and compose delta · base (0x4FE6B0, Hamilton), not
    add. Before, the clone added quaternion deltas (halving a rotation's
    animated angle: HUD_SingleRace's wobble, UI_ChooseCustomHUD's needle),
    rounded colour steps, held loop tracks past their last key and ended
    scripts only past their length.
  * Message response type 0 (0x52C7D0) sets the object's script to the
    one named by arg 1 (0x5178B0 → 0x517720) and its time (+0x10) to 0 —
    the "entry count" read for +0x10 under Message responses is the
    script's time.
  * Interpolation 3's re-basing (0x517720, **verified**, `rebased`): when
    a script starts on an object (0x5178B0, 0x51CF80, a chain step or a
    loop in 0x54CE70) every track's done bit is cleared and a track with
    interpolation 3 or 4 gets its first key's delta (the key list at
    +0x30) set to the object's current value minus the track's base
    (param 1 int, 2–4 floats, 5 quaternion via 0x4FE6B0 — operand order
    **inferred** —, 6 colour ints via 0x505580). **Open**: the other key
    list used when the track's +0x2C byte is set (0x4FE890).
  * Timed messages (`EV`, **verified**, `run_package`): each step
    0x54CE70 fires the script's events in [old time, new time), the new
    time + 1 when it equals the length (0x534C80), so a zero-length
    script's events fire on its first step and a loop's every cycle. The
    target picks the route: 0 queues the message with value 0 (broadcast),
    −4 / −5 / −6 with that value, −1 calls the host's +0x18 at once, any
    other value is an object id (`OP` +0) resolved by 0x517FE0; message
    0x1B3909AA moves the focus instead (0x52B3B0). The queue is pumped
    after the step (0x541FD0, below).
  * Screen in (**verified** for the menus): the packages' "Event Handler"
    string (0x47FF4E7C) runs INIT (0 ms) → CALL, whose events broadcast
    0xBDFD2DF9 at 0 ms and send 0x35F8620B to the screen at its end
    (180 ms in UI_Main and the dialogs, 320 ms in UI_pause). The menu
    objects answer 0xBDFD2DF9 with their FADEIN script, so their INIT →
    HIDE is followed by the fade in (the open item of the previous note;
    the clone follows HIDE now). IconScrollerMenu's handler (0x543D50)
    sets its ready byte (+0x130) on 0x35F8620B; the dialogs focus their
    Cancel_Button then (below). **Open**: what reads +0x130 (the input
    gate during the fade).
  * Screen out (**verified** for the handler 0x495B10, which switches to
    UI_CareerCrib.fng): on accept (0x0C407210), or back (0x911AB364) when
    0x404800 is false, the screen runs FORWARD on the
    Event Handler (0x537C10 → 0x51CF80, unless 0x537CD0 finds it running);
    FORWARD broadcasts 0xAADD0187 (the objects' FADEOUT) at 0 ms and sends
    0xE1FDE1D1 to the screen at 140 ms (320 ms in UI_pause), on which
    the screen switches package (0x537990) — IconScrollerMenu (0x543D50)
    runs the chosen option's action then. The Event Handler's own accept
    response does the same ([0x301 FORWARD] [0 FORWARD] [0x501]).
    **Not ported**: the clone switches screens at once; its screens do not
    run FORWARD or wait for 0xE1FDE1D1.
  * Objects the screen's code shows (**inferred** stand-in): an object
    whose zero-length INIT chains to a non-looping script (HIDE, or
    UI_pause's slot 6048A18B) and that no package message reaches keeps
    INIT's state in the clone (`ScreenState::chain_init` off), standing in
    for screen code such as 0x51DDA0 (Fade_In / Fade_Out on the cash and
    player name, 0x537E70) that the clone's screens do not all port. The
    HUD and the shop engage dialog set `chain_init` (fully native).
* **Message responses** (`MsgR`; **verified** except where noted). The
  tag test at 0x5555C9 hands the body to 0x54D1E0, a block of two-character
  tags: `Mi` (u32 message hash) starts a node (hash at +0xC, count +0x10,
  entries at +0x14), and `Ri`, `Ru`, `Rt` fill the next entry's three
  dwords: type, arg 1, arg 2 (12 bytes). `MC` (0x52AE10) and `Rs` (0x517630)
  are not traced, nor the entry array's allocation. The FOb reader's call
  (third argument 0) registers the node with 0x4951B0 (0x512120 otherwise);
  with the package's flag at +0x18 set, a node the manager already holds for
  that message is emptied and reused (0x5046D0 finds it).
  * Queue: 0x51AA20 appends {target, message, parameter, value, flag} to the
    manager's queue (+0x411C / +0x4120, count +0x4118). The pump (0x541FD0)
    routes by the value: 0 broadcasts to the objects of that hash in every
    screen, then to each screen's per-message list (0x5367F0); -2 to the
    objects of that hash in every screen; -3 to the object of that hash in
    the target's list; -4, when the target is one of the screens, does the
    -3 effect (the object of that hash in the screen's list) and then also
    delivers to that screen's per-message list (0x5367F0, block 0x54219E);
    -1 and -5 are host callbacks at +0x10C (vtable +0x18 and +0x1C); -6 sets
    the input flag (+1) for message 0x59BED120 and clears it for 0x5D4CE32D;
    any other value is an object, sent through 0x5367F0.
  * Object lookup (0x5367F0): the object's node list (+0x3C; next at +0x4,
    hash at +0xC) is searched, and the first match runs (0x52C7D0). Kinds 4
    and 6 try 0x51B000 and 0x52C760 first.
  * Entries (0x52C7D0; a MsgR entry's dwords are type, arg 1, arg 2): 0x1
    queues message arg 1 with value arg 2 (through 0x517FE0 unless -4 or
    -1, so the value picks the route); 0x2 and 0x3 queue arg 1 with value
    -1 and -5; 0x101 sets the input flag (+1) to arg 1 == 1; 0x105 queues
    0x51AF50(object, 1, the message's flag word), 0x106 (object, 1, 0xFF),
    and 0x107 and 0x108 the same with flag 0; 0x200 queues kind 3 (0x51AB20)
    with arg 1 as a name string (copied by 0x519DE0 into the node at +0xC,
    its hash at +0x10) and the object's flags, then clears the object's
    flags +0x1C to +0x28; 0x201 queues kind 2 with the object's flags and
    clears them (0x51AC10; it also copies arg 1 as the name, as 0x519DE0 does), 0x202 does so for each set bit of the message's
    flag word, 0x203 queues kind 1 (0x51ADB0) with the object's flags, sets
    every object's flags (+0x1C and +0x28) in the manager's list at +0xE4 to
    its +0x20 copy and then clears the object's own, 0x204 with no bits.
  * Focus (0x52B3B0, which 0x100 and 0x103 call): with the flag set, the old
    focus gets 0x55D1E635 and the new one 0xABC08912, each sent to the object
    and then as the -5 callback; the focus is stored at +0x8C either way.
    0x100 with arg 1 of 0 clears the focus silently; otherwise the object
    0x517FE0 finds for arg 1 takes it, and nothing changes when it finds
    none. 0x102 stores, under the object's hash (+0x10), the +0xC word of its
    +0x8C child (0 when none) in a 32-entry ring at the manager's +0x5150
    (next slot +0x514C; 0x50B300 clears an older entry with the same key).
    0x103 focuses the object that 0x517FE0 finds for the value that 0x50B360
    returns for the object's hash, else does what 0x100 does with arg 1.
  * 0x2C0 pushes a copy of the object's +0xC name onto a stack of 16 slots
    of 0x100 bytes at the manager's +0x414C (count +0x4148; 0x51B070, a full
    stack does nothing); 0x2C1 pops the top slot when the stack is not empty
    and queues it as kind 3 for the object (0x51AB20); 0x2C2 empties the
    stack (0x50B390).
  * 0x0, when the dispatcher's context argument is non-null: finds the node
    named by arg 1 (0x5046B0: the manager's list at +0x4C, hash at +0x30),
    passes it to 0x5178B0 (which stores it at +0x54 of the object it is
    called on — the object's current script — and, for a non-null node,
    runs 0x517720, which re-bases the script's tracks, see Scripts), and
    sets the script's time +0x10 to 0 (**verified**: +0x10 is the time
    0x54CE70 advances).
  * 0x300 (skips when the receiving object's current script, +0x54 →
    +0x30, is not arg 1; **corrected**, it is not a screen id), 0x301
    (skips when it is) and 0x500 (always) skip with 0x504490: from the next entry it
    counts nested 0x300/0x301 (+1) and 0x501 (-1) and stops at the first 0x500
    or 0x501 at depth 1; the dispatcher resumes after that entry. So a skipped
    0x300 or 0x301 runs the part after the 0x500 (an if/else: then, 0x500,
    else, 0x501), a 0x500 jumps past its 0x501, and 0x501 does nothing.
  * The second queue (+0x412C / +0x4130, count +0x4128) holds the kinds 1,
    2, 3, 4 and 8 queued by 0x51ADB0, 0x51AC10, 0x51AB20 and 0x51AF50.
    0x5559D0 drains it from the head (**verified**), dispatching on each
    node's kind bits. Bit 0 (kinds 1 and 3) pops the target package when its
    +0x18 is not negative: a parent that is not in the manager's list is
    logged as invalid and cleared; the node's flags are OR-ed into the
    parent's; 0x5362F0 flushes the package; the objects whose parent is the
    target then take its parent (kind 1) or the object 0x555870 returns
    (kind 3). Bit 1 (kinds 2 and 3) walks the list headed at 0x8384C4 +0x10
    to the first entry that 0x43DCC0 returns 0 for, then calls 0x555870 (both
    not traced further). Bit 2 (kind 4) sends message 0x334C5493 with value
    -4 to the target's parent, bit 3 (kind 8) to the first object whose
    parent is the target. 0x51AE80 unlinks the last kind 2 or 3 node in the second queue whose
    name hash (+0x10) is the hash of its argument (1 when found); 0x5362F0,
    the unload of a package in the manager's list, deletes the second-queue
    nodes whose object is the package and the first-queue messages whose
    object is the package or whose value 0x517FE0 resolves (each logged as
    unsafe), then releases its objects and itself (0x50B240, 0x52C510 and the
    destructor; not traced further).
  * Value 0 (**verified**, 0x541FD0): for every package, its own node list
    (+0x5C) and then each object in its per-message table (+0x6C count,
    +0x70 entries {message, —, count, objects}) that has a node for the
    message (0x5367F0), so every object answering it. The clone runs the
    pump over the one package it draws (`run_package`); responses 0, 1, 2,
    3 and 0x300 / 0x301 / 0x500 / 0x501 are modelled, the rest not.
  * The menus' INIT → HIDE objects are shown by 0xBDFD2DF9 (the Event

      model (0x61D060). It binds the channels the entity's +0x28 bits
      ask for (1 `_t`, 2 `_q`, 4 `_s`, 0x4350C0), each writing its
      compound header's frame count (+0x0A, 0x6E2110) as the length
      +0x60; with none the player is freed. The player (0x435010, rate
      +0x40 = 1): speed +0x5C = record +0x10 (0 → 1), start delay +0x68
      = +0x14 (flag 0x80), pause +0x6C = +0x18 (flag 0x100), flags +0x34
      |= record +0x0C (0 → 0x28); 0x40 takes the range +0x1C / +0x1E;
      0x200 sets the pause to r × ½ × length ÷ 30 ÷ speed and 0x400 the
      frame to r × length, where r = 0x43C170 on a fresh seed 0x69BABE69
      each time, (0x69BABE69 mod 0x7FFFFFFF) × 4.656613e‑10 ≈ 0.826; a
      record with +0x20 / +0x24 (the doors) drops 0x08 and adds 0x810.
      The root's local is the instance matrix (0x43A7A7). Playing (+0x10
      = 1) when +0x20 = 0 and +0x3C = 0.
      Update 0x435980 → 0x435140, 30 × rate × speed frames a second:
      the start delay, then the pause while the frame is short of the
      end (the overshoot carries over, fmod 0x43C240); 0x08 forward,
      with 0x1000 backward; 0x20 without 0x800 wraps by the span and
      restarts the pause, else the frame stops at the end; neither 0x08
      nor 0x10 → 0x08; 0x08 with 0x10 drops 0x10; 0x10 alone goes there
      and back (+0x08), 0x800 stopping it (+0x10 = 2) at either end and
      the pause restarting at the start. Then, unless 0x2000, only when
      the node's box passes 0x48CE10 (and no 0x827EEC / 0x827EC8 /
      0x827E98), the channels are evaluated (0x4316B0: `_q`, `_s`, `_t`,
      then 0x6E3B10) and bone 1's matrix becomes the node's local
      (0x40EFE0, dirtying it and its children, 0x6147F0). A node's world
      (0x60BB20) is local × parent's world (0x43C990 → 0x4013F0,
      row-major), the root's its local.
      L4RA has 22 such instances: the three vista searchlights
      `XO_VISTA_SPOTLIGHT_1A_DW_00` (beams 986 m tall, speed 0.025, flags
      0x28, at (−459, −470), (−232, −448), (81, −448)), a bridge
      searchlight, six jumbo planes, the tower cranes, the graffiti trains
      and the pub's sails. As with the doors their entities' own scenery
      instances are hidden (0x10, in no scenery group).
      The pose (0x4316B0 → 0x6E3B10, `Animation::bone_pose`): the
      buffer starts as the "ROOT" skeleton's (list 0x827C74, found by
      name 0x434DC0; 0x6E3C70 copies each 0x70-byte bone's scale +0x10,
      quaternion +0x20, translation +0x30). Read from the running
      original: two bones, both scale 1, rotation identity, translation
      0, bone 1 under bone 0. Channels write floats at their slots (12
      a bone: scale 0–2, quaternion 4–7, translation 8–10); each bone is
      S · R(q) · T (0x6E2D60, the quaternion not normalised) times its
      parent's; the node takes bone 1. So a missing channel keeps the
      skeleton's identity, not the entity's rest matrix (which is the
      node's local only until the first update): the vista
      searchlight 0x49C5218F (at −459, −470; only `_q`, slots 16–19)
      turns about the instance's origin at scale 1; the other two
      (0x49C52190 / 91) have all three channels on bone 0 (slots 0–10).
      The clone had posed missing channels from the rest matrix (that
      beam scaled up to ×1.4 and 23 m off).
      **Inferred**: samples past the last key are the last key; dt is
      the frame's seconds (the caller of 0x435980 is not traced); the
      bone product order (0x811E34, not traced; with the shipped data
      one of the two bones is always identity). The track window
      (`world::track_window_admits`, **verified** 0x43A4C1…0x43A526:
      r = 0x89E7A0 % 100 in [+0x39, +0x38] or [+0x3B, +0x3A]; L4RB's
      instances 3, 5, 7 and 10 set it, 20–29 or 0: free roam and drag
      tracks 4221–4223): the world is loaded before its track is known,
      so the windowed instances are loaded inactive with hidden
      placements and `World::set_track` (from the drive-in, with the
      barriers) makes them for an admitting track — shown, played, heard
      (`anim_points` skips inactive ones) — keyed by `World::anim_track`
. **Not ported**: the creation's generator draws (flags 0x400
      / 0x200, 0x43A5EE…0x43A60C). The
      doors' length is the frame count, 91 (0x4350C0 → 0x6E2110; fixed
      2026-10-31, reports: the clone had used frames − 1).
    * **Audio update (2026-11-03)**: ShopEnter1's authored CAR_AUDIO_PATTERN 3
      now drives the sound Physics context through the existing engine chain.
      Its 104 quarter-step updates and idle decay match a natural native
      capture; see `docs/evidence/nis-audio-pattern`. The clone retains the
      captured 60 Hz duration independently of render rate. Other patterns
      (including ShopExit pattern 4), scene audio gates and fades remain open.
      DynoEnter is implemented; the historical DynoExit gap is separate from
      this bounded audio change.
      **Update (2026-11-04)**: all banks 1–15, native event order, slot
      binding, scripted gates and the vanilla 30-updates-a-second scene
      cadence (the 60 above was WidescreenFix's HighFPSCutscenes) — see
      `docs/nis-audio-patterns.md`.
* **Layout** (**verified**, `frontend::layout`) — the renderer walks the
  groups (0x52C5E0; a group with alpha 0 skips its children), gives each
  group a context (0x51B7F0) and queues each object (0x51A970: alpha 0 is
  not queued) for its type's draw (0x5370B0: 1 image, 2 string, 7 movie,
  9 coloured image).
  * Transform (0x51B0B0, row vectors): v · S(size) · T(−pivot) · R(quat)
    · T(pivot) · T(position), the pivot and rotation only when the
    quaternion is not (0, 0, 0, 1) (0x4FD980 builds R); then · the
    parent group's world matrix. The canvas is that plus (320, 240)
    (0x536F70), so (0, 0) is the centre of the 640 × 480 canvas, which
    covers the whole window with x and y scaled apart (**verified**: the
    cursor maps to it as (x − left) · 640 / client width, (y − top) ·
    480 / client height, 0x5BF760, and a projected screen point as x /
    width · 640, y / height · 480, 0x4EC34C), so on a wide window the
    front end stretches (`render::ui`, the clone's "Stretched" aspect; its
    default keeps each element at its 4:3 size, centred or moved to its screen edge, see Display modes and aspect). A
    pivot is the point a rotation turns about (Minimap_North_indicator
    sits 72 above the map's centre with pivot (0, 72): it circles it).
  * Colour: per channel (own × parent + 0x80) >> 8 on the 0..255
    integers.
  * Order: an object goes to bucket ftol(its z + the parent's world z)
    clamped to 0..255 (0x51B850); buckets draw from 255 down (0x537249),
    each in fill order (**verified**): the traversal (0x536720 → 0x52C5E0)
    queues each object (0x51A970) as {object, key} at renderer +0x114
    (count +0x110), the key the pivot plus position through its view
    matrix, z; it skips alpha 0 and keys not above 0.0 (0x7D7D3C). The
    queue is sorted by the key (0x5114F0: stable LSD radix over its four
    bytes, ascending) and drawn from its end (0x50C2C0 → 0x51C670 →
    0x51B850, which appends to the bucket's list). So within a bucket the
    larger key draws first and equal keys draw in reverse queue order.
    The clone (`layout`): bucket, then key, then reverse depth-first
    order. The view matrix is the identity (**verified**: 0x536530 passes
    0x51A970 the matrix the manager's slot +0x3C fills, vtable 0x79BCE0 →
    0x50C490 → 0x43C780). The key matrix (**verified**, 0x52C5E0): the
    traversal hands a top-level group the identity and the view
    (0x536762 / 0x53675D) and a top-level object the view alone; a group
    builds its quaternion's matrix (0x504A50) with the translation row
    pivot + position + (−pivot through it) (0x52C68E), times the parent's
    (0x5187A0) — **no size**, unlike the draw transform — and hands that
    to its child groups and that × view to its objects (0x52C738). So the
    key is the z of pivot plus position through the groups' size-free
    matrices (`key_matrix`), and the clone applies the cut (keys ≤ 0 are
    not drawn; a NaN would pass). **Verified** (0x52C5E0): the queue order is
    depth first in each list's order: the traversal walks a group's child
    list (+0x64, next at +4) in turn, recurses into a kind-5 child where it
    stands and queues each other child (0x51A970) as it reaches it. Quick
    Race's highlight glow
    (DF422345, z −83 under its group's 80) is cut in its INIT state; the
    game draws it because INIT is zero-length and chains to the pulse
    0x5A8E4EBE, which puts it at z 16 and loops (chains to itself). The
    clone follows zero-length chains natively, the menus' INIT → HIDE
    objects coming back through the package's FADEIN messages (Scripts,
    "Screen in"); see the stand-in there for objects no message reaches.
    With the cut, LAN's progress cap 36D4B782 (z −15) no longer draws.
  * Images: the quad ±0.5 through the matrix (so centred on the position,
    size wide), texture corners from the state (0x536A60 → 0x51A1C0).
  * Strings (0x536F70 → 0x51C110): in font pixels through the matrix
    (size scales them). Lines step by ftol(`Sl` × the font's leading
    scale) + the font's line height; the block height is lines × step for
    `Sj` & 5, else the steps between lines plus one line height
    (0x50BF40). x starts at −width / 2 (`Sj` 1), −width (2) or 0; y at
    −height / 2 (4), −height (8) or 0. Each glyph (0x51BFC0) is
    max(width, 4) × height at the pen + its x offset, y + its y offset +
    the font's y offset, over its texture cell widened by one texel all
    round; the pen adds the kerning after the previous character
    (0x6F45F0) then the advance; widths (0x50BCE0) count the same.
    Fonts by name hash (0x51BDC0, table 0x7F918C): the Korean and Chinese
    Conduit fonts take a y offset of 18–23 and leading scale 2 or 1; the
    rest 0 and 1. Font 0x9583AA1A is drawn × 1.6 when 0x7F70D0 is 8 or 9
    (not modelled: English only).
  * Text is the label's string unless flag 2 (then `St`, 0x536F70).
  * **Open** (seen in `game --shot` main, quickrace, options_display,
    carlot, parts, crib, pause, results; `NFSU2_SHOT_MS` sets the front
    end's time and `NFSU2_SHOT_SIZE=WxH` the target): UI_QRTrackSelect's
    track picture is not drawn (the slot's white template now follows its
    scripts and no longer shows; the screen's code that sets the track's
    image is not traced); faint dark specks at glyph
    cell edges (the widened cells sampling neighbouring glyphs) are not
    compared with the game's sampler state.
  * The HUD's position row ("1st /4", RacePositionNumber `Sj` 0xA and
    RacePositionNth / NumberRacers `Sj` 8 at −224 + 59) is bottom aligned
    over the lap row (LapText / LapNumber / NumberLaps `Sj` 0 at −158.25 −
    3), which hangs from just below it.
* **Resources** — textures by `bin_hash` of the upper-case name without
  extension (TPKs in FrontB, GlobalB, GLOBALA, LANGUAGES/LanguageTextures);
  fonts likewise (`ConduitMdITC_TT21i` is in GLOBALA, the rest in
  LANGUAGES/English.bin). The untextured image's request hash is
  `bin_hash("(UNTEXTURED SIMPLE IMAGE)")`.
* **Strings** (LANGUAGES/English.bin, 0x39000) — u32 16, u32 count, u32
  table offset, u32 text offset; a 256-entry character map (applied by
  0x50D3C0, see "Native front-end fixes, part 1"); the table
  {u32 hash, u32 offset} sorted by hash; NUL-terminated Latin-1 text.
* **Fonts** (0x30201; **verified** against the renderer, 0x51BDC0,
  0x51BFC0, 0x6F45F0) — name at +0, texture name at +0x100, `FNTF` at
  +0x200: +0x0A glyph count, +0x0C flags (0x40000: 16-byte glyphs, else
  12), +0x14 glyph table, +0x18 kerning table, +0x24 i32 line height,
  +0x40 / +0x44 1 / texture size (+0x12 is not the line height: 16
  against 20 for ConduitMdITC_TT14i). Glyph (16 bytes): u16 code, u8
  width, u8 height, u16 x, u16 y, u8 —, i8 x offset, i8 y offset, u8
  kerning count, u16 first kerning pair, i16 advance. Kerning pair n at
  table + 4 + 4n: u16 previous character, i8 adjust, u8 —.
* **Menus** — every menu is an IconScrollerMenu (vtable 0x79C0FC) in its
  own package; each option is `0x51F680(icon texture hash, label hash, 0)`
  with an action vtable whose second entry handles the accept message
  0x0C407210. The option sets and their conditions:
  * UI_Main (0x4AEE30): Career → UI_StartCareer (0x4AED80), Quick Race →
    UI_QRModeSelect (0x4FC050, game mode 2), Online, LAN, Customize (mode
    0x20), Profile Manager → UI_ProfileManager, Options → UI_OptionsMain
    (mode 0x10).
  * UI_StartCareer (0x4AF110, title set to "Career"): with a saved career
    (career +0x20, 0x502FE0) whose intro movie has played (0x86347C,
    career +0x873C, saved) "Resume Career" + "Start New Career", saved but
    not yet played "Start New Career" acting as resume (the resume vtable
    0x790CC0, which "Resume Career" has too; the new career's is
    0x790CB8), without one "Start New Career"; always "Load Game"
    (0x790CC8). **Verified** 2026-10-30. Resume (0x495A30) sets game mode
    1 and goes on from the career's state.
  * UI_CareerCrib (0x4AF820): Return to Explore Mode (Yes/No "Return to
    Explore Mode?"), World Map (only when 0x862838 > 1), Car Select →
    UI_CareerCarSelect, Change Parts, Performance Tuning / Dyno (Yes/No
    "Do you wish to Performance Tune / Dyno your car?"), View Rewards →
    UI_CribRewardOptionsMain, Save, Back to Main Menu (Yes/No "Are you
    sure you want to quit to the main menu?").
  * UI_pause in explore (0x4C2900) and in a race (0x4C2BD0), UI_postrace
    (0x4BEE10): see `screens::explore_pause_menu`, `race_pause_menu`,
    `post_race_menu` for the exact sets and conditions (World Map only for
    races started from it, 0x85BA67; Restart; Return to Explore Mode in a
    career; Options; Quit to Main Menu).
* **Garage scene** (GarageMain.fng; `garage.rs`, `draw_garage`): the 3D
  scene the front-end menus stand on. **Verified** unless marked.
  * Who pushes it: UI_Main (descriptor 0x7F7DC8, factory 0x4ED6B0 →
    constructor 0x4DF140) sets game mode 2, builds its icons (0x4AEE30),
    copies a ride into the FE car 0x8371B0 (0x413440 at 0x4DF264) and
    pushes GarageMain.fng when it is not up (0x555F60), else hands the
    garage the new car (0x4D8C70). The ride: the preset DDAY_PLAYER_CAR
    (0x637280) while the byte 0x86347D (career +0x873D) is clear, else
    0x515D00(0, ride, 0). **Inferred**: +0x873D (set by 0x500BD0 and
    0x541550, cleared by the new career 0x532840) means the player has a
    car of their own and 0x515D00 gives it; the clone shows the profile's
    car when it has one, else the preset. 0x8371B0 itself starts empty
    (static constructor 0x40C910: 0x610280(−1, …)).
  * The empty turntable after boot (gaps row 7): under Wine (live
    reads) 0x8371B0 holds the preset's type (0x16) as soon as UI_Main is
    up and the car shows 10–20 s later; wined3d runs the game clock at
    ~13 % of real time, so the original's asynchronous car load is slow
    there, not empty by design. **Inferred**: the load path after
    0x4D8C70 is not traced.
  * Platform: the front end's load (0x57FE85) opens SHOWROOM.BIN when its
    first screen (0x8384C8) is UI_Main.fng or none; otherwise a visited
    shop's scene file (0x863444 and 0x86344C set, `FRONTEND\PLATFORMS\%s`
    with the shop record's +0x40), else CRIB01.BIN once (0x8635B9, set by
    0x53CCD0 and 0x55A7D8), else SHOWROOM. 0x4A7180(from, to) swaps them
    later (crib 1 → 4 at 0x4AFAD0, back 4 → 1 at 0x4AF464). A platform file
    holds a solid list (DISC01–03, flag 0x40; BACKDROP; BACKDROP_FLOOR,
    flag 0x40; PLATFORMBASE), its texture pack and an environment pack
    XPOS … ZNEG, which 0x5B9920 copies into the static cube 0x87088C
    (called by 0x4A7180 after its load; **inferred** for the first load,
    whose caller is not traced). The clone gives the car that cube.
    Without the faces (**verified** in the code): 0x5BCAE0
    binds 0x87088C without a null test; it exists whenever 0x870CB8 ≠ 0
    (0x5BA4F4: 256², A8R8G8B8, managed), and a missing face copies
    DEFAULTALPHA's 1024 zero bytes over the face's first row only. So the
    cube is the last platform's (top rows zeroed), or its creation
    contents (black, **likely**) before any. A car renderer now starts
    black (`car::start_envmap`; the clone had a made-up night-sky
    gradient). `garage_car_renderer` keeps the front end's one cube
    across platforms (`fe_cube_texels`): a platform without its six faces
    leaves the previous platform's cube with each face's first 1024 bytes
    zeroed (`car::envmap_without_faces`; the shop fixes). Every shipped platform has
    all six faces (`showroom_has_the_scene_models_and_an_envmap`).
  * Model handles: 0x493600(hash) on GarageMain +0x70 PLATFORMBASE, +0x88
    BACKDROP, +0xA0 / +0xB8 / +0xD0 DISC01–03, +0xE8 LOCK (string
    0x797C18; not in Showroom.BIN), +0x100 BACKDROP_FLOOR: it stores the
    hash, links the handle into the list 0x82DBC0 and resolves the model
    (0x48DF90, 0x48D780).

    0x32C72D8F → view +0x220 = 1, 0xFC946BFA → view 4, the road
    reflection; nothing while +0x1C8 is set). Matrices are row-vector

    angle `(int)(deg·65536)/360`). View 1: BACKDROP and BACKDROP_FLOOR at

    has moved on by the integer 1200 at 0x7F45D0); a car change turns the

    verified unless marked): UI_CareerCrib (0x4AF820) checks GarageMain.fng

    current field of view, target, eye (+0x80 / +0x90 / +0xA0 → +0xC0 /
    +0xD0 / +0xE0) and takes the record's (+0x100 / +0x110 / +0x120,
    record +0x30 / +0x34 → +0x130 / +0x134), then 0x44D190(p10, p11) sets
    the duration +0x14C = 0.0055 (0x78710C) × the largest of |p10 − p11|
    (0x4A55E0 passes +0x274 and the record's angle; 0x453320 0, 0),
    |Δfov| ÷ (50 dt), |Δ+0x130|, |Δ+0x134| ÷ (50 dt) and |Δtarget|,
    |Δeye| ÷ (2.2 dt) (0x4455D0; 0 for unchanged ones), dt the frame time
    0x865194, at least +0x150 (0.3 for a part view; 2.5 back to the base,
    0x453320). 0x44CE00 (state 0) adds dt to +0x148, f = +0x148 ÷ +0x14C
    (1 at the end or with no duration), s = (sin(f·180° − 90°) + 1) ÷ 2
    (a binary angle, 0x75BED4 / 0x43C2B0), and lerps field of view,
    target, eye (and +0xB0 / +0xB4) by s; state 2 when done. The car
    (0x4C1D40: +0x124 = camera +0x14C; +0x11C the angle, +0x120 the
    shorter of the up and down distances from the angle mod 360 to the
    record's, a tie going down, +0x138 the way; +0x12C / +0x130 steer and
    its difference; the right-stick rates +0x248 / +0x24C zeroed) turns
    linearly: f = +0x128 ÷ +0x124, angle = +0x11C ± f · +0x120, steer =
    +0x12C + f · +0x130 (0x4D8A85…0x4D8B09), only while camera +0x30 is
    set, so a reset (0x453320 clears it) stops the turn where it is.
    `NFSU2_SHOT_MS=250 game --shot parts_hood` shows a view mid-blend. Slot 0x44 (engine paint) also opens the hood (0x61F830 on the
    FE car, GarageMain +0x160/+0x15C), closed again on the next view.

  * **Fast switching** (verified; Wine at full speed, UI_QRCarSelect,
    0x8363F0 read every 30 ms): the lots never ask GarageMain for a car at
    the key. Each step stores the tick clock 0x8651A8 (crib 0x4B04C0 at
    +0xB8, UI_CareerCarLot 0x4AFFA0 at +0xE0, UI_QRCarSelect 0x4E2590 at
    +0xC4, which Customize's car select shares) and the screen's tick
    (0x4DFFEC, 0x4EE00D, 0x4FCD1D) hands the selected ride (0x511E00) to
    the loader (0x4D8EC0 → GarageMain 0x4D8C70 → 0x4D8030) once
    (now − it) · 0.00025 ≥ 0.3 (0x784268, 0x78758C), then clears it. The
    loader (GarageMain +0x234): 0x4D8030 cancels a load in flight (+0x2CD0,
    0x63AE10 on +0x2CC4) and starts the new one, unless the old car is
    still held by a swing (0x836408 with 0x83640C clear), when the ride is
    queued (+0x23D0, +0x2CD8 = 1; a later one overwrites it); 0x4D8180
    marks it loaded (+0x2CD4); 0x4D82D0 state 1 swaps it in (0x4D8220) and
    swings (state 2) when its car type differs (+0x2CE0, 0x4D8030: ride +0
    ≠ the shown one's), else goes straight to state 3; state 2's end
    loads the queued ride (state 1, 0x4D8030(+0x23D0)). So the old car
    stays until the new one is in, every swing turns a whole 120°, and
    the last car asked for ends in front: five Lefts 0.14 s apart gave one
    swing 0.53 s after the last key; Rights 0.45 s apart gave three
    swings back to back (0x8363F0 240 → 0 → 120 → 240). The clone did
    the swing at each key and restarted it from wherever the platform
    was, so fast keys left the car off the front disc (and a filter change
    could index a car of the new list); now `Game::garage_request` waits
    the 0.3 s on every lot, holds a car asked for during a swing until it
    ends (the last one wins) and keeps the shown car itself
    (`garage_crib_shown`), swings only for another car type (a crib
    placeholder always: 0x4A7930 / 0x4A7960), and `View::changing`
    reports a swing under way. The clone's car load is in the frame
    (`draw_garage`), so its state 1 lasts no time. Tests: the selftest's
    `selftest_lot_hammer` (Quick Race's and Customize's car selects and
    the D-Day car lot: 160 random steps 0–0.6 s apart, the car in front
    at every frame at rest, the selected car shown at the end) and
    `garage::tests::car_changes_wait_for_the_turn_so_the_car_ends_in_front`.
    **Open**: 0x4E8530 / 0x4F2E41 (vtable 0x797A38, a 0x4F9D90 subclass
    built by 0x4FB320) do the same on +0xC4; which screen it is was not
    found; a QR filter change's own load (0x4EED10) is not traced (the
    clone waits the 0.3 s for it too, **inferred**).
  * **A lot's first car swings too** (observed; internal notes):

  a cubic Hermite over 0.3 s (0x574E40). No wrap at the ends (0x51FA00).
