## Front-end particles, performance brakes, shadow pull (2026-10-29)

Side-by-sides: $OB_PRIVATE/wine/compare/fe72/. **Verified** (REA
decompiles of SPEED2.EXE) unless marked.

* **Front-end particles.** A platform file is an ordinary bundle: its
  emitter descriptions (0x35021) join the resident list 0x830D08 after
  GLOBALB's (0x491C70) and its placed emitters (0x35020) are bound by name
  hash and started (0x48BC00, 0x48BC50). SHOWROOM.BIN holds one,
  D4884E83 `XEFE_Showroom_SmokeA_01` at (−3.57, 9.55, 0), state 1, no
  switch: 10 particles a second, life 6 s, speed 0.75 ± 60 %, cone 60°
  (mode 0), gravity −0.3 (rises), drag 0.2, texture SFX_SMOKE_B_CS
  (0x0DE39984), which only FrontB.lzc and InGameCommon hold (the front
  end's resident pack is FrontB). GarageMain's update FEGarage_UpdateCarTurn
  (0x4D82D0, at 0x4D8A48 while its +0x1C8 is 0) runs Particles_Update
  (0x492E10) with the frame's dt, and the frame's particle draw
  (Particles_Render 0x48BDF0, 0x5CAEC8 / 0x5CAED3) shows them: the steam
  plume left of the car on every SHOWROOM screen. Clone: `Platform::load`
  fills the platform world's `emitters` / `placed_emitters` (GLOBALB's
  descriptions, then the file's; the missing textures from FrontB.lzc) and
  `draw_garage` runs and draws them (`GarageScene::fx`); a `--shot` starts
  as the scene stands `NFSU2_SHOT_MS` after the menu asked (at most 10 s).
  The other platforms' emitters are loaded the same way (not compared).
* **Particle direction, mode 0** (+0x18 = 0; 0x492539…0x492633,
  correcting the earlier "every way"): the three turns about x, y, z are
  each `rand · cone − cone / 2` degrees (+0x50; [esp+0x50] = +0x50,
  [esp+0x58] = +0x50 · 0.5 at 0x4920FF / 0x492148, × 65536 (0x784238)
  through `_ftol`, / 360 into the 16-bit angle), applied to the emitter's
  z axis: a jitter of ±cone/2 per axis. The clone drew a full turn per
  axis, so the steam spread along the floor instead of rising.
  **Inferred**: the order the turns compose in, the exact draws.
* **Brakes from the performance parts.** 0x6399E0 (run by 0x639CF0 —
  0x4D80F2 … 0x521410, whenever a ride's parts or performance change, and
  from GarageMain when 0x8A1CD0 is set) sets, with ride +0x2F0 the
  performance block (fitted flags at +0x50 + id, 0x599620): slot 0x1B
  (ride +0x5FC) to the car's part of level 1 when part 0x28 (the level-1
  brakes' third) is fitted, else 2 with 0x29, else 3 with 0x2B, else level
  0 (0x61BC90: the first part of the slot at that level, 0x61B990; none
  keeps the slot); and slot 0x0D (+0x5C4, ENGINE) to level 3 when the
  level-3 engine, ECU and turbo packages (categories 3, 7, 4; 0x599640:
  every part of the package fitted, or no such package) are all on, else
  2 for the level-2 ones, else 0. Then 0x61BCE0 refreshes the shown slots.
  The brake draw (0x62DF85…0x62E091) takes all four brakes from slot
  0x1B's models (+0x1B08 + 0x10·group + 4·lod): front group 0; rear
  group 1 when the part is level 0 (the stock brakes' rear model), else
  group 0 (BRAKE STYLE01–03 have one group); slot 0x1C is never drawn.
  Rachel's 350Z (performance level 2: parts 38, 39, then 41 replacing 40,
  42 — see the preset note) so shows BRAKE STYLE02 (C6578696, cross-drilled
  disc and caliper), as the original's main menu does; the clone showed
  the stock disc. Clone: `car::perf_visual_parts` (in `Car::load_tuned`
  for every in-game car, and for the front-end car in
  `Game::garage_request` with the profile's or the preset's parts),
  `Preset::perf` now fits as 0x5A64B0 does. Test
  `rachels_brakes_come_from_the_performance_parts`. **Remaining**: the
  disc is darker than the original's (its lighting, not traced).
* **Shadow pull**: see Car shadow (player 0's camera mover type).
* **Sky cycle**: see Sky, "Shipped behaviour" — 0x870D14 is 1 at run
  time (the options object's static constructor), the cycle runs, and the
  clone now runs it by default.
* **Quick Race car select, floor reflection (view 4), checked against the
  original's render target** (d3dretrace of t1.trace under Wine with
  `-S 10639750`, the 320 × 240 target after the car's opaque parts:
  wine/compare/fe72/qrcars-reflection-view4-orig-left-clone-right.png).

## Help bar in the career and in game, package init, in-game dialogs (2026-10-29)

Checked against the original under Wine ($OB_PRIVATE/wine/runs/<run>,
capture.py with PEEK; side-by-sides in $OB_PRIVATE/wine/compare/menus73:
`orig/` the original, `clone/` the clone, `before/` / `after/` the clone's
front-end screens before and after the flag-0x40 rule). **Verified** (REA
decompiles and the objdump) unless marked.

* **Package init hides flag-0x40 objects, in every package.** 0x54E4B0
  ("Init Package %s") runs the visitor 0x51C870 (vtable 0x79AB94) over the
  package: an object flagged 0x40 gets 0x50CA00 (flags |= 0x400001 — the
  hidden bit, down a group's children too) and loses 0x10000000. On PC that
  drops the console footers ("Select", the $JOY_EVENT_ glyphs) and the
  screens' own name / cash group (e.g. UI_CareerCrib's group 000E53DA,
  flags 0x40000040, holding EB406FEC / EB3A688A): the clone drew "$0" there
  on the garage and the shops. The clone applies it in `layout` (`hidden`:
  flags & 0x41, unless the screen's code shows the object). The screens'
  base constructor 0x551DF0 writes the package's own EB406FEC only online
  (0x8500D0 ≥ 0xC).
* **The career's name / cash alternation** (`screens::HelpCycle`): see the
  doc comment there. 0x537E70 (from the bar's constructor 0x551F90 and
  from 0x54E6F0 in game mode 1 for a mask with bit 1 and not bit 2) →
  0x51DDA0(name, cash, 0.75, 5.0): +0x34 name, +0x38 cash, +0x3C the one
  shown, +0x40 0.75 s, +0x44 5.0 s, +0x48 the countdown in 0.25 ms ticks
  (× 4000 + 0.5, 0x577320 counts it down by g_FrameDt × 4000); Fade_In on
  the name, Fade_Out on the cash; texts "%s" of the profile name and
  "%$d" of 0x861E74 (grouped, no '$': the HUD's Bank shows "0" the same
  way under Wine). The tick 0x537F60 (on 0xC98356BA, handler 0x55BBDD)
  swaps them when the countdown runs out: the cash for 5.0 s, the name for
  0.75 s, each switch Fade_Out / Fade_In (0x54C20A66 / 0xBCC00F05, 320 ms).
  The cycle starts once (only while +0x3C is 0) and runs on across
  screens. g_GameMode (0x850078): 2 from UI_Main's constructor (0x4DF18B),
  1 at the career's start (0x495A3D, 0x4C5033), 0x20 Customize, 8 online,
  0x200 LAN; the clone keeps it in `Game::game_mode`.
  **Inferred**: the cash shows 5 s and the name 0.75 s (the constants'
  order is as traced; no capture of a career screen with the bar yet —
  the D-Day intro has none reachable without driving to the car lot).

* **The explore pause's "Replay"** (0x4C2900): after Options (shown when

## Speech and music archive (SDATA/sdat.viv; 2026-10-29)

Ported in `src/formats/viv.rs`, `src/audio/{schl,microtalk,ealayer3,
mp3_tables,speech,music,streams}.rs`; tests `tests/speech_music.rs`, the
selftest's "streams" step, probe `devprobes/src/bin/speech_probe.rs`.

* **The archive** (**verified** unless marked): a "BIG4" (header kind 3 of
  0x6FA8D0; 0xC0FB → 1, "BIGF" / "Shp" → 2; header size u32 BE at +0xC,
  entries from +0x10: offset, size (BE, width = the 4th character, at
  most 4), name) with 10 files: speech/UG2_Speech.{csi,evt,idx,big},
  speech/nisaudio.{csi,evt,idx,big}, pfdata/MusicSFx.{mus,mpf}. The audio
  start-up 0x486510 looks for `sdata/sdat.viv` in the install folder, else
  under the CD path (0x458890), makes the big-file device (0x6F6750: one
  archive slot of 0x120 bytes, 12 open files of 0x20), puts its name at
  the front of the search path (0x6F6E7A with 1: the vtable +0x30 call
  leaves its pushed 1 as the second argument; 0x6F6DB2 splits the path
  at ';') and mounts the archive (0x6F67D7: 0x40 bytes, the header size
  0x6FA93B, the whole header kept, "BF Header", realcore big_vfs.cpp).
  Opening (0x6F69E6): "bf:" and one leading '/' or '\' dropped,
  "archive|name" picks an archive, else the archives in mount order; the
  entries in order (0x6FAA2E), names compared without case (0x6FA8A0 →
  0x75DED8), separators not folded. The game's own file calls (0x57CA20 →
  0x6F8710) go through the default device (0x6F78DC: no ':' and no
  leading slash), so the archive is searched before loose files
  (**inferred**: the default device's walk was not decompiled).
* **Streams** ("SCHl" / "SCCl" / "SCDl" / "SCEl" chunks, size LE incl.
  the head; "PT" tags as the banks'): the codec class of 0x728DF9 —
  10 EA-XA (the NIS bank, stereo 32 kHz; blocks: +8 samples, +0xC a u32
  per channel, the history carried across blocks), 4 / 0x16 MicroTalk
  (the speech bank, mono 22050 Hz), 0x17 EALayer3 (the music, stereo
  32 kHz). Decoder setup: 0x72CB4B (MicroTalk 0x7328E8 / 0x732B10 /
  0x732BE1), 0x72428B (EALayer3 0x728744 / 0x728469 / 0x72820C).
* **MicroTalk** (0x7343F3 frame, 0x733A9E excitation, 0x733BC8 LPC,
  0x733C54 synthesis, 0x73432C header, 0x734798 output; tables 0x819208
  coefficients, 0x819308 codebooks, 0x819508 commands; state 0xD68
  bytes): see `audio::microtalk`. In a stream block each channel's data
  starts with a byte: non-zero = a header follows (the first block),
  then per frame a marker byte (0xEE: after the frame a BE offset, count
  and that many BE samples overwrite it; state +0xD64, 0x73478B with the
  version > 1). With a lag over 216 the first subframe reads below the
  codebook into the state before it (history, coefficients, gains).
* **EALayer3** (`audio::ealayer3`; tables 0x7D0C30 Huffman trees in the
  mpg123 form, 0x7D0CC0 linbits, 0x7CF620.. alias coefficients, 0x7D1600
  the synthesis window as −32768 · D[32j + k] for k ≤ 16, each row
  twice): per EA frame a byte 0 / 0xEE, then MSB-first the MPEG header
  byte (version, rate, mode, extension), the granule index, scfsi with
  granule 1, per channel part2_3 (12) and 47 more side-info bits, the
  main data, padding; 0xEE frames end with {offset, count, count ×
  channels BE samples} played after the granule (**inferred** from the
  block sample counts, 1152 + 47 = 1199); a 0xEE frame with header 0 is
  that PCM part alone; a 0 byte with header 0 ends the block. Blocks
  hold 2304 samples (4 granules); song 0 decodes to 198.2 s. Output
  (**measured** under Wine): on the MMX path (0x8B4A2C set) the
  granule's 576 subband floats become 16-bit values at 0x72FD95 (×
  16384.0, `fistp`, low 16 bits; the largest seen 22389, no wrap) and the
  fixed-point synthesis 0x730C66 (pmaddwd with 0x7D11E0, >> 13,
  `packssdw`) gives 16-bit PCM that **saturates**. Against the clone's
  decode of the same 16.3 s of song 0: scale 0.99997, residual 7 LSB rms,
  3420 samples at the limits where the clone's float runs past full
  scale. The clone rounds to nearest and saturates (`ealayer3::pcm16`);
  the bit-exact fixed-point path is **open**.
* **Speech banks** (`audio::speech`; loads 0x482A00 NIS, the code at 0x484352 the
  speech bank by language table 0x7ECFA8; completion 0x45AF90 →
  0x45A7C0): `.csi` "MOIR" switch names → ids (bank word 0x1A4B NIS,
  0x721E speech; NIS: SoundFX_Select, NIS_Select_End, NIS_Select_Crowd,
  NIS_Select_Start, as the exe's table 0x7ED01C); `.idx` +0x54 the entry
  count, entries {flags, size, offset, base in the .big}; an entry
  (0x738A20): u16 id, +4 key count (bit 7: played bits), +5 records, +7
  unit − 1 (× 256 bytes), +8 u16 end, records {BE16 offset, keys}; the
  played-stream callback 0x485B10 → 0x484060 adds the entry's base and
  starts the stream (0x7227A3) on `speech/nisaudio.big` (speech object
  +0x38). `.evt`: per event a play step after the dword 0x46439: 3, the
  entry, the constraint count, {mask, component} pairs. Selection: a
  record fits when each key's bit is set in its switch component &
  mask (**inferred**, see the module). NIS events: 0x4000 → 0x4023
  (race starts, NIS_Select_Start set by 0x45A6D0 with the IntroNis flag
  and the camera track's bit), 0x4011 → 0x4024 (NIS_Select_End: endings
  EndingNis0n → 1 << (n − 1), n ≥ 3 → 4; the dynos 0x100, the shops
  0x200; then 0x4000 entering / 0x8000 leaving / the camera track's bit;
  then 1 — tables 0x82BA78 / 0x82BAF8 built by 0x45B160 from "IntroNis%d",
  "EndingNis0%d", DynoExit, ShopExit1, DynoEnter, ShopEnter1), 0x4014 →
  0x4025 (4 × 30.6 s), 0x400E → 0x400E (23 short mono lines). Volume
  (0x484060): the stream's level byte / 127 (0x723E9D).
* **In-game speech** (UG2_Speech, MicroTalk, 857 lines in 14 entries,
  10 events on the switches Career, Career_Magazine, Career_Dvd, Outrun,
  Time, FE_Screen, FE_OptionScreen, Intro_Area, Intro_Events,
  FE_Dynoshop; the exe's name table 0x7ED0DC). Who speaks, when and which
  line: **Rachel's speech** below (2026-10-30; ported).

* **EA Trax** (`audio::music`): the `.mpf` ("xDFP" v4): 162 nodes, 79
  events, 43 streams in bank 0 (layout set up by 0x73A7C0: slot +0x38
  nodes, +0x40 events, +0x4C banks, +0x50 stream table). Song i →
  event i (0x7399E0 on the event table, **verified**) → node 3i (type 1)
  → node 3i + 2 (type 4) whose stream id is **1-based**: song i plays
  table entry id − 1 (song 0, Riders on the Storm: id 39 → entry 38,
  373.6 s; **verified** under Wine by the recorded output's waveform,
  normalised correlation 0.98 while the title showed its caption — the
  old 3i + 2 → entry 39 rule played another song). Events 27–78 are
  the interactive score (table 0x7ECC10 per context +0xB4: 0x1C the
  front end, career shops 0x16–0x1D by the shop visited, 0x46B330; in
  game the "Ambience" parameter map), played in part by the clone
  (Sound effects audit, Round 3).
* **Music manager** (0x482350 each frame → 0x482180 → 0x47B080 /
  0x47B260; player states 0x47AC50 on +0xC0, **traced**): in the front
  end (audio +0x90 = 1) with the menu music level and a menu-mask song
  → EA Trax (0x47B080), else the interactive piece (0x47B260); in game
  EA Trax when game music and master are on, the race mask has a song
  and it is not a drag (0x89E7D8 / 0x890108, 0x4018F0) or drift race
  (0x89E7D9 / 0x890104, 0x401910) — those get the interactive score.
  A new song starts only when none plays (0x82AFD4 = −1, the stream
  ran out or was stopped) — songs never loop, the end of one starts the
  next of the playlist (0x46B6F0: the jukebox order 0x83ACB8 with the
  mask, sequential from +0xA8, or random among the not yet played with
  +0x9C; the remaining mask +0x88 / +0x90 refills when empty) — and in
  game not while PC_Loading is up (0x4A9330) nor with no flow. States:
  1 start (front end, 0x480C30), 2 stop on leaving the game (0x481440 →
  0x47AF40), 5 pause (0x739030(…, 1)): the flow's PRERACE / PAUSE /
  9 (0x481210 with 3 / 6 / 9), PC_Loading over a running flow, any
  game state but 3 / 6, a movie in game (0x8383AC); 6 resume; 7 stop
  on the flow's LOADING / CAMERA_FLYBY (0x481210 with 1 / 2); 0xB stop
  for a movie in the front end, back to 1 after it (a new song). The
  playing song's caption: Chyron_ShowSong. **Clone**
  (`streams::MusicContext`, `Game::music_context`, `Streams::
  music_frame`, `Mixer::pause_track`): front end / game / paused /
  stopped as above; a track load stops the song (`begin_loading`), the
  countdown and pause menus hold it, in-engine scenes stop it in game
  (the front end's pass, 0x47B080 with audio +0x90 = 1, has no scene
  test), a drag or drift race has no music (its interactive score is not
  ported). A scene goes with its track (`Game::drop_drive`). The dyno
  (L1, internal notes): audio +0x90 = 5, the in-game rules with
  the front end's pool (0x46B6F0 for g_RaceType 8); its song plays through
  DynoEnter and is held by the Quit question (flow message 7). **User bug
  fixed** (2026-10-30, "silent after a while, also in the menus"): Quit
  to Main Menu from the pause left a running scene behind (Esc during
  the career's start scene, a race's start scene or a shop scene), and
  the scene test stopped every front-end song until the next city start;
  checked with `--flow soak` (below). Likewise Return to Explore Mode
  from a race's pause kept the race as paused, and every menu after it
  (the garage, the shops, the SMS screens) held the song (`Paused`),
  silent for good once the speech ended: a city start now ends any race
  (`Game::explore`). A decoder thread that dies marks its buffer done
  (`streams::Decoding`), so no track can wait for samples for good. The
  playlist is the clone's own
  (`music::next_song`: table order after the last song, either side, no
  shuffle; 0x46B6F0's per-side positions and random mode are **not
  ported**), every song has a stream (song 0..26 → events 0..26 →
  streams, all 27 decode in full).
* **Audio check aids** (game.rs): `NFSU2_AUDIO_WAV=file` runs the real
  mixer offline on game time for `--shot`, `--selftest` and `--flow`
  (`-` for no file); `NFSU2_AUDIO_METER=s` with it prints every s seconds
  of game time the output's peak and RMS with the mode, music context,
  song, volumes and the mix (voices, tracks, levels), dropping the
  samples so a run can last hours; `NFSU2_AUDIO_STALL=1` a device that
  never plays; `NFSU2_AUDIO_DEBUG=1` the live game's line every 2 s.
  `--flow newcareer` (`NFSU2_FLOW_LOAD=profile`, `NFSU2_FLOW_SMS=esc`)
  plays the career menu's first option as a player keys it and logs the
  D-Day script, inbox and car; `--flow soak` runs `NFSU2_SOAK` phases
  (`menu:s`, `career`, `career_esc`, `drive:s`, `race`, `race_explore`,
  `garage:s`, `quit`, `profile`); `--flow dday` the selftest's D-Day
  save paths alone. Each flow gets a fresh save folder, or
  `NFSU2_FLOW_DATA=dir` (a copy of the profiles; never the player's own). The selftest covers the player's paths:
  `selftest_dday_paths` (a D-Day save's career menu, Resume with the
  script over, Start New Career with the instruction in the viewer, Esc
  and Quit in the start scene with the menu's songs after) and
  `selftest_music_after_race_pause`.
  **Open**: the interactive score, the fades (0x459990 over 300 ms
  between interactive pieces), the shuffle option's source.
* **Volumes** (0x45C210, the options +0x24.. × master × 32767 as mix map
  fields): the clone scales effects (one-shots, loops), engine (the
  granular voices), speech (speech tracks), menu / game music (music
  tracks) by the option × master (`mixer::Levels`); the mix map's own
  ducking of these fields is not applied (**open**).

## Rachel's speech (2026-10-30)

**Verified** in the binary (objdump; REA's Ghidra provider did not start:
no Java) unless marked. Ported in `audio::speech` (`Picker`, `lines`,
`Bank::fit`), `audio::streams` (`say`, `stop_speech`, `speech_free`),
`frontend::dday` (`Hints`, `Script::step`) and game.rs (`say`,
`speech_free`); tests `dday::tests`, `speech::tests`. Under Wine with the
audio driver off the speech object 0x82BA30 is 0 (peek), so every speech
call is skipped and Rachel is always "free": the lines themselves cannot
be checked there; the hint slots and clocks were (below).

* **The line objects.** No hint object is kept: each caller builds a
  two- or four-dword object on its stack, {vtable, +4, +8, +0xC}, whose
  vtable is a one-entry table (0x79AD04 → 0x510F10, 0x79AD08 → 0x510F30,
  0x79AD0C → 0x510F50, 0x79AD10 → 0x510F70, 0x79AD14 → 0x510FA0, 0x79AD18
  → 0x510FC0, 0x79AD1C → 0x510FE0, 0x79B870 → 0x510ED0), and calls it on
  the speech object +0x2C when 0x82BA30, 0x7FAAA8 and +0x2C are all set.
  The methods set one switch's tuple (0x735880 on its block, adding the
  switch with 0x735800 the first time) and, when the speech stream object
  (0x82BA30 +4) has no request pending (+0x44 = 0), queue stream kind 3
  (0x46CA60(3, 0x45B480, 0)); 0x45B480 → 0x45AD40(3) starts the request
  in place of what the stream plays and frees it (+0x44 = 0). Tuples
  (`speech::lines`): 0x510ED0 Career (1, +4, +8); 0x510F10 Time (4, +4);
  0x510F30 FE_Screen (2, 1, +4, +8); 0x510F50 FE_Dynoshop (2, 0x20,
  +4, +8) (0x46D580 registers 0x7ED124 = FE_Dynoshop; FE_OptionScreen,
  0x7ED10C, is only registered by 0x4587A0 and never set); 0x510F70 Intro_Events (0x10, +4, +8 or +0xC by
  Rand_Int(2)); 0x510FA0 Intro_Area (0x20, +4, +8) (0x46D480); 0x510FC0
  Career_Magazine (1, 0x200, +4, +8); 0x510FE0 Career_Dvd (1, 0x400, +4,
  +8); 0x46D2D0 Outrun (x, +4, +8) with x 1 → 3, 2 → 1, 4 → 2, 8 → 4,
  0x200 → 5 (0x510EF0 calls it with 8: the tuple is (8, +4, +8, m(+8)),
  verified in the disassembly 0x46D2D0–0x46D336).
* **Rachel's outrun lines** (2026-10-31, race2; **verified** in the
  disassembly; ported: `Hints::outrun_start` / `outrun_end`,
  `lines::outrun`, game.rs `rachel_outrun`). Both run on the hint object
  (career +0x887C) with the line object {vtable 0x79AD00 → 0x510EF0, a,
  b}, each after Speech_Stop 0x45B490 and only when 0x82BA30, 0x7FAAA8
  and its +0x2C are set; the random draws (0x43C1C0) are made either way.
  Start (0x607190 → 0x532E40 → 0x511000): with +1 set, pick =
  Rand_Int(5) kept at +0x1A, (a, b) = (1, {1, 2, 4, 8, 0x200}[pick])
  (table 0x7993C8); else (0x20, 0x200). End (0x541330 → 0x5110C0(won),
  after the bank, 0x529BE0 and the magazine triggers): with +1 set, r =
  Rand_Int(2), a = won ? (r ? 16 : 8) : (r ? 2 : 4), b = the table at
  +0x1A; else a = 0x40 won / 0x80 lost, b = 0x200, and +1 is set (so +1
  is also "an outrun line was said", besides 0x524340's DDAY_EVENT_A).
  Not heard under Wine (no speech object with the audio driver off).
* **Which event and record** (**verified** in the disassembly and ported,
  docs/native-fixes/N-AUD2.tsv: `speech::Library`, `Streams::say` / `play_nis`). A
  setter stores its switch's tuple (0x735880); the switch's listener
  0x738630, installed per switch by 0x7386A0 from the `.evt`'s switch
  table (switch i → event i), posts the request {event key, the event's
  +0xB values} (0x736920): it passes when Rand(100) ≤ event +9
  (0x73698A) and waits in the channel's queue (0x736860: lifetime +2,
  priority +4; **not modelled**, the clone evaluates at once). 0x738340
  (from 0x7385B0) skips an event at its channel's count limit (+8 & 0xF;
  none of the requested events has one), orders the alternatives
  (0x737470: count +6, alternative k at event + 4 · u16[+0xC + 2k],
  weight (b & 0x1F) · 4^(b >> 5) (table 0x819A94 = 1, 4, …, 0x4000), one
  Rand(total) per non-zero weight, zero weights last in file order) and
  tries them in that order: Rand(100) < alternative +1, the switch masks
  0x7382A0 (+8 >> 4 of them) and the key fit 0x738DD0 (+7 keys; the game
  callback 0x50D510 answers 0), then 0x7377B0: per step (alternative +2
  >> 2 steps at alternative + 4 · byte[+8 + j]; +2 & 3 a channel mode)
  0x737030 resolves the entry and 0x737230 lists its records: 0x7371C0
  (each constrained key's union against the request value), per record
  0x736F30 (constraint j against key j: a bit of its mask and of request
  value (component − 1); components 0 / 0xFE any, 0xFF the state table)
  and 0x737140 (enable bits); a record within the entry's last +6 plays
  (0x735D70, the ring after the key table, written by 0x735D30 from the
  play step 0x737EEB) is only kept as the fallback played longest ago,
  used when nothing else fits. The first alternative with candidates
  plays; a request that fits nothing plays nothing (the retry hook
  0x8B5158 is never set). The shipped banks use one alternative per
  event (weight 0x39 = 100, chance 100, one step, no keys, no switch
  masks, no channel modes, no state components; all ten / four events
  chance 100), so the gates pass and draw; the rings: FE_Screen's entry
  0x2D keeps 1, the five outrun entries 0x28 keep 7. Each setter's
  switch event is the one the clone's old first-fit search happened to
  find for every setter tuple (1376 tuples compared), so the change is
  the draws before the pick, the rings, and the NIS bank's lines now
  picked at random among their fitting records (THUNDERSTRM 9,
  CollisionStream 6, BLOWNENGINE 4) instead of the first.
* **The pick** (0x737B20 → 0x738860, **verified**): a candidate slot
  holds the entry (+4), its first fitting record (+8) and their count
  (+9); the record is first + pick(count, entry). The generator 0x738750
  (five words 0x819AB4…0x819AC4 summed with carries, the counter
  0x819AC8) is seeded by 0x738940 from the library start 0x736180 at
  each speech-library init 0x486220 (0x4866EA with 2, 0x486A6D with 1 —
  the latter on every world entry, a draw read under Wine at 0x486A31): the first
  init's seed is the game's draw Rand_Int(0xFFFFFFFF) on 0x7EA624
  (0x4866F0 / 0x486A2C, through 0x43C140), each later one the last seed
  + 1 (0x82BA34, .bss 0 — not a static 9), taken as |seed| (
  `Library::init`; the game's call is listed for review, until then
  the clone keeps the seed 10). 0x738860 avoids the last min(n / 2, 10)
  picks of the same entry (history 0x8B5688, 32 × {index, key}, ring
  0x8B5708; 0x738800), at most 32 draws; with key −1 it makes one draw

## Renderer performance: what the clone may skip, merge or reorder (2026-10-29)

The performance pass changed how the frame is recorded, never what it
draws: the shots and the benchmark's frames are byte-identical before and
after (the proof is in README.md, **Performance**). The rules it relies on:

* **A draw that puts no pixel on screen may be left out.** `PassCull`
  (render/mod.rs) drops a group of instances (the draws of one solid in
  one section with one set of flags and LODs, which share their
  instances) only when it is wholly outside a plane of the view, or when
  the vertex shader's scenery cull (`cull_size` in world.wgsl, 0x5D6580 /
  0x5D64E0) drops every one of its instances — tested on the CPU with a
  margin, so an instance near the threshold is always left to the shader.
  An instance with the hidden flag (0x10, in every view's cull flags) is
  dropped by every view.
* **Bounds.** An instance's sphere is its solid's sphere moved by its
  matrix and scaled by the matrix's largest singular value, not its
  longest column: 1,514 of Bayview's 48,317 placements have a 3×3 that is
  not a scaled rotation (up to 1.24× the longest column). The road
  reflection (view 4) flips each prop about its own origin (m22 negated,
  0x5D67B4), so its groups have bounds of their own (`mirrored_bounds`);
  it is culled by the main view's planes (it shares view 1's camera and
  projection, 0x5C30F6 / 0x5C7ED0).
* **The cube faces** (views 0x10–0x15, near 0.5 and far 64: 0x7FEE88 /
  0x7FEE8C) clip at their far plane too; together they see the cube of
  ±64 m about the eye in the camera's axes, so a frame's candidates are
  found once and each face tests only those. The face schedule is the
  game's (0x5C397B, table 0x7FEEA0, periods 0x7FEE90): at the top update
  setting (rate 3, row 12) all six faces every frame, so the clone keeps
  six; rates 1 and 2 already render fewer (`display::env_faces`).
* **The world shaders' height discard was never taken.** `clip.x` is
  f32::MIN in every pass (main, reflection, cube faces, garage), so
  `world_z < clip.x` never held; with it gone the shaders without the
  alpha test have no discard and keep the early depth test on every GPU.
  worldheadlight's projector texture is read only where its light falls.
* **Independent passes may change places.** The cube faces now go to the
  GPU before the motion blur: they share no target or input. The frame's
  command buffers are recorded on several threads but submitted in the
  recording order, after every `write_buffer` their passes read.
* **Post passes merged** (each exact on any GPU):
  * motion blur's StretchRect copy of the back buffer (0x5CC470) is not
    made: the first blur reads the scene itself, the same 8-bit texels;
  * the streak buffer's decay (ZERO / BLENDFACTOR, 0x5CBB6A) multiplies
    its source by zero, so its pass reads no texture (`fs_zero`), and the
    first frame's clear is a clear;
  * a one-tap copy followed by an ONE / ONE add of the streak buffer (into
    the back buffer, or screen copy 1 when only the streaks are on) is one
    pass, `fs_add`: the sum of two 8-bit values, saturated, is what the
    blend unit makes of them;
  * motion blur keeps a uniform slot of its own, so the end-of-frame
    passes' uniform writes never touch what the scene reads.
  Not merged: passes whose 8-bit intermediate the next pass reads (the
  bleach bypass's three, overbright's half-size chain, the blur rounds):
  folding them into one shader would need the conversion to 8 bits
  emulated, which no API pins down to the last bit at a tie.
* **Car draws.** A part's matrix and light context are made once for all
  its draws, and the draws of parts the car's LOD leaves out get no
  values (the shader never reads them); every car renderer of a device
  shares car.efx's shader, layouts and pipelines (`car::CarShared`).

### Allocator and PGO (clone only, 2026-10-31, decisions155)

Nothing here is the original's: SPEED2.EXE allocates from its own pools
over the MSVC heap (e.g. 0x575630 `jmp _malloc`, the pool allocator
0x440D40). These only change how fast the clone's loaders get memory and
how its code is laid out; no frame, sound or save byte changes.

* **Allocator** (`src/allocator.rs`, README "Allocator"): mimalloc (fast)
  by default; the system allocator when the machine has under 10 GiB of
  RAM or under 4 GiB available at start; `NFSU2_ALLOC=fast|lean|system`
  forces one. Picked once at the first allocation and kept.
* **PGO** (`scripts/pgo.sh`, README "PGO"): an optional build that
  trains on the benches. The normal `cargo build` does not use it.

## Native profile saves and the Profile Manager (2026-10-29; checked against the original under Wine)

Code: `src/formats/native_save.rs` (container, payload offsets),
`src/frontend/profiles.rs` (folder, list, current profile, MC texts,
migration), `Profile::from_native` / `to_native` and `NativeContext` in
`career.rs`, `Settings::apply_native` / `write_native` in `options.rs`,
`McList` / `McMessage` in `screens.rs`, `McAct` and `mc_*` in game.rs.
Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/native_saves/*.sav` (written by SPEED2.EXE),
tests `tests/native_save.rs`, selftest `selftest_profiles`.

* **Where** (**verified**): 0x4A9C40 calls SHGetFolderPathA(0, 0x801C =
  CSIDL_LOCAL_APPDATA | CSIDL_FLAG_CREATE), CreateDirectoryA, appends "\" and
  the name at 0x7F66A0 (→ 0x78E8F4 "NFS Underground 2"), CreateDirectoryA,
  hands the root to the memory-card library (0x6FC01E → 0x6FCCFE) and counts
  its entries with FindFirstFileA "\*". Each profile is the file
  `<root>\<NAME>\<NAME>` (no extension); seen under Wine at
  `drive_c/users/<user>/AppData/Local/NFS Underground 2/NAME/NAME` with the
  widescreen fix's CustomUserFilesDirectoryInGameDir off. The library deletes
  with DeleteFileA (0x760B0C) and RemoveDirectoryA (0x760AE2). **Clone**:
  `$XDG_DATA_HOME/NFS Underground 2/<NAME>/<NAME>` (else
  `~/.local/share/…`): the XDG data directory is Linux's local-application
  data, and keeping the game's own folder name and layout lets a profile
  folder be copied between Windows/Wine and the clone unchanged.
* **Container** (**verified** by the reader 0x6FD3F0…0x6FD6E8, the header
  constructor 0x6FC226, and by the original loading a file written outside
  the game): header 0x1C bytes — +0x00 "20CM" (0x4D433032), +0x04 the file
  size, +0x08 section 1's size (8), +0x0C section 2's size, +0x10 / +0x14
  their checksums, +0x18 the checksum of header bytes 0…0x17; section 1 =
  the block type 0x10D and the payload size (0x4D9C15 / 0x4D9CBF; 0x4A9850
  loads only type 0x10D with the expected size); section 2 = the payload,
  always 0xD692 bytes (0x52A450 = 0x5B9690's 0x43E + 0xD254), so every file is
  54966 bytes. The checksum 0x6FE173 (via 0x6FCD1C): CRC-32 poly 0x04C11DB7
  (table 0x8145E0, the standard MSB-first table), register = NOT of the first
  four bytes read big-endian, then each further byte shifted in from the
  right (`r = (r << 8 | b) ^ T[r >> 24]`), result NOT; fewer than four bytes
  give 0. The reader sets error 8 on a bad size, magic or header checksum and 7 on a short
  read (+0x2E0); 0x4A9850 then posts 0xF35D144E instead of 0x461A18EE.
  The two sections' checksums are computed too, but a mismatch's error 8
  (0x6FD6E8 / 0x6FD718) is cleared at 0x6FD73C, so such a file loads
  (**verified**: three community saves edited without fixing the payload
  checksum load under Wine with their values). The clone does the same.
* **Payload** (writer 0x52A290 on G + 0x10 = 0x83A9E0, reader 0x5344E0 — the
  same order, **verified** byte for byte against a running original's
  memory): offsets are payload offsets.
  * 0x0000 garage 0x83AD90 (0x5166B0 / 0x516850; **verified** by the
    writer and, for the records named, by the fixtures). Every record is a
    car object with a vtable at +0 (not saved; 0x79B134 for the full ones)
    and one head saved from +4: +4 a dword (0 in every save), +8 the id
    hash (0x503510 / 0x503680 match it; 0 = free), +0xC the car's raw
    performance rating (0x516C42: 0x5B69A0(0, −1), not scaled; 0 until the
    car's object is built — the stock list's entries get it on the car lot
    or the Customize car select; the 206's 196.7, the Corolla's 144.12 =
    the rating minimum), +0x10 usable, +0x14 the Quick Race filter bits (1
    Stock, 2 My Cars, 4 Career, 8 Sponsor, 0x10 Ranked; 0x5162D0).
    0x0000: 48 stock entries (garage + 0x1C·i, the head only, 24 bytes;
    +0x14 = memory +0x18 the list index, −1 free), 0x480 their count
    (+0x540, 0x1F). 0x484: 20 "My Cars" records (garage +0x544, stride
    0x434, 0x430 bytes saved): head, car record (memory +0x18, 0x418),
    memory +0x430. The main menu's Customize makes one (0x5165E0 takes the
    first free; seen under Wine: filter 2, a generated id, the 206's car
    record with the new front bumper; the race record's +4 then names it).
    0x5844: the five career slots, 0x7F2 bytes each (memory +0x5954,
    stride 0x7F8, 0x516620): +0x00 the head (+4 = bin_hash("CAREER_SLOT_n"),
    filter 4), +0x14 the car record, +0x42C memory +0x430, +0x430 locked
    (+0x7F4), +0x431 has its own car (+0x7F5), +0x432 0x3C0 bytes from
    memory +0x434 (X) by 0x503F00, remapped: X+0…+0x15C as is, then
    X+0x15C (16), X+0x16C (0x100), X+0x26C (16), X+0x27C (16), X+0x28C

    brand hashes), X+0x29C (16). Those are the owned-part bit sets

    counting with 0x61B990 for the part's own car; see "Owned visual

* **What the clone maps** (`Profile::from_native` / `to_native`,
  `Settings::apply_native` / `write_native`): name, bank, stage, races
  entered, intro flags, driving time, the cash pickups' flags, the visit
  table (events won = state 1, milestones 1 / offered 2, world challenges 1,
  shops visited +4), the stage records (unlocked = below the stage,
  outruns, reputation, the signed sponsor, the three win lists), the
  legend's show flags (`Profile::map_hidden`, the In-game World Map's
  hidden groups; they were per session before), the D-Day event, the saved
  place, the five slots (locked, car, its parts against the stock ones,
  fitted / owned performance parts, uniques, brands, spent, the five dyno
  settings — `CarSlot::tuning`, kept in career.txt's `slottuning` lines
  before and lost in the native file), the current slot (once the player
  has a car), the inbox; the options above, the EA Trax play mode included
  (`Settings::trax_random`, shown on the jukebox and flipped by its
  triggers). A Quick Race record or a player's settings the clone did not
  change keeps its bytes (Free Run's record holds 0 laps, which the clone
  reads as 1). Every other byte is kept from the file the profile was
  loaded from (a new profile starts from the original's own fresh profile,
  the same bytes in three runs; since R8 written from its rules by
  `career::fresh_payload`, docs/exe-tables.md). A car the
  original has not put in a slot gets a record of the type hash and its
  stock parts only (paint and the rest of a ride's record **not traced**).
  A slot whose car type the clone does not know keeps its car flag and
  record as loaded, and no profile is written when the car types failed
  to load (`NativeContext::check_writable`).
  Since 2026-10-30 (profiles107) also the owned visual parts and My Cars
  (see below). Not kept natively and so lost on save: its random state
  0x7EA624 (not in the save), the trigger counters 0x864210 / 0x86420C
  (not in the save; globals whose only writers are 0x5338D0's increments
  0x533964 / 0x533A2D, so the original never resets them while it runs;
  the clone keeps them for the session and `Profile::load` carries them
  over a Resume or Load), the main-menu car
  when it is not a My Cars record or a stock car, and the total
  reputation (the clone sums the stage records'). The display options and the key map stay in the clone's
  options.txt (the original keeps the display options in the registry,
  0x5BEA30; the keyboard map is not in the profile).
* **Round-trip tests** (`tests/native_save.rs`): five saves written by
  SPEED2.EXE under Wine (career_start, car_lot, garage, mycar — a fresh
  profile after Customize fitted a front bumper to the 206 — and options —
  then the play mode Sequential, track 1 Racing, player 1 Manual,
  difficulty Hard, a key remapped) parse and rewrite byte for byte, load
  into the clone's profile and options and write back unchanged; options
  differs from mycar in exactly the four option bytes; the garage records
  sit where the writer puts them; slot tuning and legend flags reach the
  file and come back.
* **Community saves** (2026-10-31): 44 distinct profile files from
  playground.ru (EU and US builds, stage 0 to 100 %, edited ones too) are
  all the same 54966-byte format and load (three with a wrong payload
  checksum, which the original accepts: see the container above). The
  original under Wine loaded each and saved it again from the Profile
  Manager; its resave differs from the input only in the four hint dwords
  the loader zeroes, the checksums, and (one save) a controller block of a
  device not attached, and the clone's load and save (career and options)
  gives the original's resave byte for byte for all 44 (`finished_resaved.sav`, test `clone_rewrite_matches_the_originals_resave`;
  the community files stay out of the repo, no redistribution terms:
  `NFSU2_COMMUNITY_SAVES=dir` runs `community_saves_rewrite_as_the_original_resaves_them`
  on `<name>.sav` + `<name>.resave.sav` pairs). Found by them: the visit
  table's +4 of a won event or milestone is often 0 in a finished career
  (the finished-career save: 48 events, 3 milestones; won from the World Map's list or
  edited); the clone sets +4 only when it changes the entry's state
  itself, and keeps the file's otherwise.

* **Boot** (**verified** under Wine): one profile → it is loaded and "Load
  complete." shows after the title's Enter; two or more → MC_List "Load"
  with the names in name order; none → "Would you like to create a new
  profile?". The clone does the same after the splash (`boot_profile_step`).
* **UI_ProfileManager** (options 0x4C58B0, **verified**; as shown under Wine):
  Create, Load, Save, Delete, always all four. Each opens MC_Main through
  0x4A3100: Create mode 0x861 (operation 0x60), Load 0xC11 (0x10, callbacks
  0x3A2BE557 / 0x8867412D), Save 0x4A51 (0x50), Delete 0x831 (0x30). MC_Main's
  start 0x4F3570 dispatches the operation (table 0x4F36B8 → 0x4F3690): 0x10,
  0x30, 0x70 list the profiles (0x4E8CE0: memory-card state 8); 0x50 with a
  profile copies its name and goes to state 5, without one leaves at once
  (0x461A18EE); 0x40 / 0x60 the create flow (message 0x5A051729). The
  states (0x4E8D30): 1 "Creating a new profile will …" (0xD36620FE), 2
  "Would you like to create a new profile?" (0x02B641C0), 3 the name
  editor, 5 "Are you sure you want to save^the profile named %s?"
  (0x2A9BA6F9), 6 save (0x4D9AB0), 7 save over (0x4D9B80), 0x7000000 "You're
  over the limit of saved profiles…" (0xB786AF76; the limit is **not
  traced**). Observed flows: **Load** → MC_List → with a profile current
  "Loading a profile will result in the loss of any unsaved changes to the
  current profile. Are you sure you want to load a profile?" (0x81B1D73D,
  Yes / No, No focused) → "Load complete." / Continue → back to the Profile
  Manager (the main-menu car changes to the profile's). **Save** → state 5 →
  "Do you want to overwrite previously saved game?" (Yes / No, No focused) →
  "Save complete." / Continue. **Delete** → MC_List "Delete" → "Are you sure
  you want to delete NAME?" (Yes / No, No focused). **Create** with a
  profile → state 1 (No focused), Yes → the name editor (see MC_Main above).
  All in MC_Main.fng under the header "Save/Load" (0xB19F8B41). The
  library's own texts are memcard/LOCALE_<LANGUAGE>.loc ("LOCH", "LOCI",
  "LOCL" + count + offsets from the LOCL tag, UTF-16LE): 2 Yes, 3 No, 4
  Continue, 6 the overwrite question, 7 "Save complete.", 8 "Unable to save
  %1.", 9 "Load complete.", 10 "Unable to load %1.", 11 "Are you sure you
  want to delete %1?", 12 "Save game deleted.", 13 "Unable to delete %1."
  (what the original shows after a confirmed delete is **not** observed; the
  clone shows text 12). MC_List.fng: header 0x426C7B4D and title row
  0x48D4FCAE = the operation's name, rows option_name_1…8 (0xB2980BA8…, y
  −130…150) with backings 0x66E29936…3D, the title row's arrows
  0x44496A03 / 02 hidden.
* **Save points seen in the original** (Prompt, the default after profile
  creation): the car lot asks "Are you sure you want to save the profile
  named NAME?" right after a stock car is taken; the garage (UI_CareerCrib)
  has a Save item; the Profile Manager's Save. No save at Start New Career or
  at the D-Day garage goal. Ported 2026-10-31: see **The save points**
  below.
* **Leaving the garage** (**verified** and **observed** 2026-11-01,
  small171, a community stage-6 save with Prompt and Autosave on):
  "Return to Explore Mode?" Yes runs 0x4AF360: 0x52A4D0 compares the
  profile with the snapshot the garage's INIT took (0x4AF515 /
  0x4AF4C2, 0x52A470(0): only with save prompts on, profile +0xA108 =
  0x844AD8, and unless one is kept; the snapshot pointer 0x851148 was set
  in the garage and 0 in the city) and asks the save point (0x4A3100 mode
  0x151) only on a change, else 0x9A3B571D → the city. Under Wine: from
  Resume Career and from Jump to Garage, unchanged, straight to free roam
  (twice); after a Car Select in the garage, "Do you want to overwrite
  previously saved game?" and then "Are you sure you want to save the
  profile named Sawa?". The clone does the same (`LotDeal::LeaveCrib`,
  `changed_since_snapshot`; selftest: a change in the garage asks, none
  goes straight). **Open**: the player's report of a question the clone
  skipped was not reproduced; a change made before the garage's INIT
  (outside it) asks nothing in either game.
* **Help bar**: the profile name (EB406FEC) is the current profile's; the
  original showed the loaded profile's name there at once.
* **Migration** (clone only): on start, when no native profile exists and
  `<app>/career.txt` (Overbright's folder) was never migrated, it is read with the old
  parser, written as `NFS Underground 2/<name>/<name>` (name filtered to
  letters and digits) with options.txt's profile options, and the marker
  `<app>/migrated-to-native` is written; career.txt and options.txt
  are left in place.

### Profile names, settings before a profile, owned parts, My Cars (2026-10-30, profiles107)

* **Profile names and case** (**verified**; `profiles::resolve` / `find`
  / `exists`, `McAct::SaveAsk`, `Profile::save`). The name editor's key
  handler 0x551280 takes Backspace, Enter, Escape and, through
  0x4FF310, letters (a–z, A–Z) and digits for the profile entry (kind
  +0x204 = 6; kinds 4 / 5 also take @ . _ / space , @ ., kinds 0 / 3
  Latin-1), up to 7 (+0x20C), **as typed**: no case is changed. No
  uniqueness check runs in the editor or at the "save the profile named"
  question; the memory-card library decides: the save (state 6, 0x4D9AB0
  → 0x6FBFC1) writes through the file layer 0x6F9BFC (CreateFileA on a
  temporary file, MoveFileA onto `<root>\<NAME>\<NAME>`; folders by
  0x6F975C), whose name lists compare with _stricmp (0x6F9AE6, 0x6F9988),
  on Windows' case-insensitive file system. Under Wine (a private Wine copy,
  :143): with the profile NAME on disk, Create → "name" → Yes asked "Do
  you want to overwrite previously saved game?" (the library's text 6);
  Yes wrote into NAME/NAME (same folder and file name, the payload's
  name now "name"; the help bar showed "name", MC_List the folder's
  "NAME"). So a name that differs from an existing profile only in case
  is that profile. The clone finds folders and the file inside
  case-insensitively (an exact spelling first), asks the overwrite
  question for such a name, and saves a loaded profile back into the
  folder it came from. Load, save, create (the overwrite question),
  delete and the boot all go through `profiles::resolve` / `find`; the
  original has no rename (a name typed over another's in any case is
  that profile, as above). What is shown: MC_List the folder's name (as
  under Wine), the help bar and the save question the payload's own name
  (profile +0, `NativeSave::name`). **Clone choice** (design note):
  folders that differ only in case (possible on Linux only, e.g. "the finished-career save"
  and "the finished-career save" made by older clone builds) are one profile: listed once,
  as the folder whose profile file is the newest (equal times: the exact
  spelling, then name order), and every operation uses that folder; the
  others stay on disk untouched (nothing is merged or deleted
  automatically; deleting removes the chosen one, and the next newest is
  listed then). Tests: `profiles::case_tests`, `tests/profiles_case.rs`
  (own XDG_DATA_HOME), selftest `selftest_profiles`.
* **Settings before a profile is loaded** (**verified**; `Settings::load`).
  The options other than the display ones live only in the profile: the
  profile object's settings start as 0x5116E0's defaults (every volume
  1.0 but S+0x2C 0.7, Random play mode, …; a new profile runs the reset
  0x515AA0 → 0x515800 again); the registry holds only the display values
  (0x5BEA30 / 0x5BEEB0, `settings.reg`); nothing loads the last profile
  early — the boot reaches the profiles only after the splash (one is
  loaded, several are listed). So the boot movies, the splash and the
  profile list play at the default volumes. The clone wrote every option
  to options.txt and applied the last profile's at boot (a profile with
  the music at 0 gave a silent first loading screen and no EA Trax
  caption); options.txt now holds only the display options and the key
  map, and the rest come from the current profile or the defaults.
  Old options.txt files are still read whole once, for the career.txt
  migration (`Settings::load_text`).
* **Owned visual parts** (**verified** by code, not yet against a save
  with parts bought; `NativeContext::owned_bits`, test
  `owned_parts_round_trip`): 0x503D50 / 0x503DB0 set / test a part's bit
  except in slots 0x3F, 0x44…0x47 and 0x49. 0x503B10: n = 0x61BA90(part,
  car, slot, 0, −1), the number of parts 0x61B990 walks before it (any
  hash, any level; the slot's first group, then its second, 0x6101F0),
  where car is the car type whose name hash is the part's group
  (0x610020 → 0x610140, its +0x840), else 0x2E — one past the 46 types;
  **inferred**: its name hash matches no group, so only the slot's
  shared groups count; then table 0x503CAC → 0x503C90: slot 7 X+0x26C, 9
  X+0x294, 0xC X+0x27C, 0x1D / 0x1E X+0x16C, 0x20 X+0x28C, 0xA2 X+0x29C,
  each + 4·(n >> 5); others X + 4·category (0x501D70); the bit n & 31.
  X = the slot's memory +0x434, saved by 0x503F00's remap
  (`native_save::OWNED_REMAP`). The clone sets the bits of the parts it
  owns and clears those of the parts it does not; bits that name no part
  of the car stay.
* **My Cars** (**verified** unless marked; `Profile::my_cars`,
  `career::MyCar`, `Game::qr_cars`; test `my_cars_load_and_write_back`):
  saved records are 0x430 bytes from memory +4 (+4 the id, +8 the rating,
  +0xC usable, +0x10 the filter bits, +0x14 the car record). Main-menu
  Customize (game mode 0x20, UI_QRCarSelect): Accept needs a free record
  (0x5165E0, +8 = 0), else the dialog 0x558580(…, 0x639, …, 0x91921A8D);
  then 0x552CD0(3, …, id): a stock car (0x516360) gets a new record, id
  bin_hash("TUNED_CAR_<index>") with filter 2 and usable 1 (0x52A720 →
  0x516B90), marked made (0x839BC2); a My Cars record is customized
  itself; 0x502A40 makes the id player 0's car (race record +4). Back to
  the car select (0x55BE00) runs 0x521110: a made record whose 0xAA
  parts all equal the stock car's (0x50E900) is cleared (+4…+0x10 0,
  +0x14 = 2, the car record zeroed) and player 0's car becomes the
  stock entry's id. Stock entries' ids are bin_hash("STOCK_<car>")
  (**inferred** from the fixtures: "STOCK_PEUGOT" = 0x959B1E16).
  UI_QRCarSelect lists the garage records whose filter bits meet the
  filter (All Cars 3 = stock 1 + My Cars 2); the clone lists the stock
  cars, then the My Cars records (**inferred** order), skips empty
  filters, and races a My Cars record with its parts. A record the clone
  makes holds the car type, every slot's part and the fitted performance
  parts (paint data and the rest **not traced**, zero). Delete Tuned Car, the Quick Race customize path, the Ranked
  cars and Back to the car select: see the next section.
* **Not done** (open): see the next section (2026-10-31) for the records,
  the save points, Delete Tuned Car and the Quick Race customize path.

### Save points, records, Delete Tuned Car, clone saves in the original (2026-10-31)

**Verified** (REA / objdump of SPEED2.EXE) unless marked; Wine runs on a
private copy `$OB_PRIVATE/wine/runs/<run>` (wined3d, Xvfb :161).

* **A save the clone wrote loads in the original** (**verified** under
  Wine): the test `write_a_clone_save_for_the_original` (ignored; writes
  `$NFSU2_SAVE_OUT`) takes garage.sav and adds owned visual parts (rims,
  slot 7, 9, 0x40) with two of them fitted, two My Cars records
  (TUNED_CAR_0 a 206 and TUNED_CAR_1 a Golf, each with a non-stock front
  bumper, the Golf a performance part), player 0's car = TUNED_CAR_1, the
  intro played (career +0x873C), every shop visited and entered (visit
  table +4 / +6 = 5) and Rachel's hints changed (+4, +9, +0xA). The
  original booted it ("Load complete."), its main menu showed the Golf
  with the bumper, Customize's car select opened on it with both records
  and "Delete Tuned Car" on the help bar; the Profile Manager's Save then
  wrote a file equal to the clone's but for 9 bytes: Rachel's hints
  +0x108, +0x110 and +0x118 (career +0x8984 / +0x898C / +0x8994), dwords
  the original zeroes between load and save (the driving-time reading
  +0x110 among them; who clears them is **not traced**). Clone records
  made before this round lacked the paint: a new car record now holds the
  car type's stock paint (+0x84C) in slot 0x3F and the vinyl colours
  0xD0561E94, 0xD0561E8D, 0x44D28FAE, 0xD0561E8C in turn in 0x4D…0x5C, as
  the original's new records in car_lot.sav (240SX) and mycar.sav (206)
  do (**inferred** from those two: the setter is not traced; test
  `a_new_my_cars_record_has_the_stock_paint`).

  copies the whole payload (0x52A290) to +0x16778 (0x851148) unless one

  current profile's payload in memory up to date without the file (the

  `Profile::load` reads the payload in memory first. So the clone no
  longer writes the file at its own points (race wins, purchases, SMS…):
  as in the original, progress reaches the disk at the save points
  above, the Profile Manager's Save, or never (Save option Off).

## Hidden races, engage tips and cash pickups (2026-10-30; checked against the original under Wine)

**Verified** (REA decompiles of SPEED2.EXE) unless marked. Checked in the
original (Wine copy, new career at the airport, memory read and written
with /proc/pid/mem): the World Map, a tip and two pickups (below).

* **Hidden races** (event +0x7F ≠ 0: the 32 `S<n>_H_*` events and
  STAGE_0_CIRCUIT_0). Their marker is in the marker table like any open
  event (0x533320 does not test +0x7F) and in the world (the trigger, the
  Engage key, its XEE_EVENT_* effect from 0x605790), but never on a map:
  0x532C30 (the event test of 0x533120) is false for +0x7F ≠ 0; else the
  event must be in the open list (career +0x71C8, 0x5007E0 by +0x08) and,
  for an SUV event (+0x0D = 1), a career slot must hold an SUV of the
  player's own (0x5278A0: slot +0x7F5 and car type +0x88A). 0x533120 (a
  marker entry: shop → 0x513110's tests, event → 0x532C30, milestone →
  0x501150, challenge → 0x5135A0) is the filter of the in-game World Map
  (0x4E0512), its legend (0x4EE4A9) and the minimap's marker test
  (0x4CA7C0); the minimap's item builder 0x4EC8C0 drops failing events
  before an item is made, so with the GPS on (0x4CA6D0's stage-0 / GPS
  target branch) they are not shown either. Nothing changes +0x7F: being
  found, an SMS (ENGAGE_TIPS_HIDDEN only pays its tip) or a win do not put
  them on a map; a won event leaves the open list. The front-end World
  Map list (UI_CareerWorldMap, 0x4B1360) does not test +0x7F (a track
  list, not a map). **Under Wine**: at the intro the open list held
  CA207584 (circuit), 1BCB7AB0 (sprint) and STAGE_0_CIRCUIT_0 (CA207583,
  +0x7F = 1), all three in the marker table; the World Map showed Car Lot,
  Circuit and Sprint with one circuit icon, none at STAGE_0_CIRCUIT_0's
  marker (353, −485). (The original opens those stage-0 events during the
  D-Day intro; the clone's `refresh_open` opens none then: a difference
  outside this work, **open**.) Clone: `Game::event_on_map` filters
  `world_entries` (minimap) and `map_icons` (World Map and legend).
* **Engage tips** (the in-world SMS markers): route triggers of kind 0x12
  (56 in ROUTESL4RA's 0x3414A; boxes at z 0), each named by a
  condition-15 message (+0x08; 42 messages ENGAGE_TIPS_* and
  ENGAGE_TIP_CAREER_PROG, mailbox 2 Game Tips, icon 9, +0x0C the cash: 25,
  or 50 for FILTER, HIDDEN, TRLBRK, ORGANIC; CAREER_PROG is urgent). There
  is no stage gate: every tip whose message is unsent is live from the
  start of a career. The player update 0x5EB050 (career free roam, no
  replay, no world challenge 0x501690) each frame takes the first kind-0x12
  trigger holding the car (0x5D9C00(car +0x60, 0x12, 0)) to 0x532D50 →
  0x529C50 (see SMS): the message arrives once (0x514CB0 finds it in the
  inbox afterwards; 0x529600 adds it, unread, new flag set), its +0x0C
  goes to the bank (career +0x7134) and 0x528990 relists the tips at
  career +0x600 (128 pointers): each kind-0x12 trigger whose message
  exists and is unsent (0x514E10). That list is only read by the marker
  effects (0x605790 kind 1, XEE_GAME_TIP: the nearest listed trigger under
  200 m, at its +4 / +8 / +0x14, z 0 → the ground). No map shows them (the
  minimap and World Map take only the marker table, 0x500EE0). Their

* **Cash pickups** ("banks"): career chunk 0x34A1E (59 records of 12
  bytes at 0x838430, count 0x838434, loaded at 0x512D82): +0x00 (u16) the
  cash, +0x02 the condition (1: the stage 0x862838 above +0x04; 2: the

* **Second pass (2026-10-30, markers103; side by side with the original
  under Wine, wined3d on Xvfb, car moved by writing every copy of its x, y

  * Engage tip: ENGAGE_TIPS at (1713, −846) seen from 30 m (slot 10,

  * Cash pickup (501, −808), driven through: bank 0 → 50, flag byte 1 of
